repository.readme:
Tedix

Website · Docs · Discussions

**Hand off the work. Tedix brings back only the decisions that need you, and handles the rest.** ## The problem If you use AI assistants for real work, this probably sounds familiar: - You explain your company again in every new chat, to every tool. - An assistant says "done", and you can't see what it actually did. - You copy results by hand from one assistant to another. - Requests for your OK are spread across many open chats, so you keep checking on them. - Two people, or two assistants, end up doing the same job. ## What Tedix does - **One shared list of work.** People and assistants work from the same list, so everyone sees who owns what and nothing is done twice. - **Context that follows you.** Your company's facts, your preferences and past decisions reach whichever assistant you use: Claude, ChatGPT, Codex or Tedix's own. - **A record of every step.** Each piece of work keeps what was used, what came out and who said yes. - **Decisions one card at a time.** What needs you waits in one short stack, the Deck. Clear it on your phone or at your desk. Everything else goes to a timeline, the Feed, that you read when you want to. - **It stays yours.** Your goals, your decisions and what your team taught the assistants belong to your organization, even when you change models or tools. Tedix's own assistants are called **tedis**. A tedi has one job, its own memory and only the access you give it. It asks before anything risky, and nobody can approve their own request. ![A supplier folder in a Tedix OS workspace](docs/public/assets/tedix-os-supplier-review.png) _A tedi reviews one supplier folder, writes a decision note that cites its sources, and asks before sending anything. Run the small version in [examples/supplier-review](examples/supplier-review)._ ## Examples of recurring jobs - **Find conversations worth joining.** A tedi looks for public threads, for example on Reddit, where your product could help, and drafts a reply. You get one card per thread: post it, edit it or skip it. - **Match invoices against stock.** A tedi compares supplier invoices with what actually arrived and shows you only the mismatches. - **Act on critical error reports.** A tedi summarizes a new error report, finds who owns the problem and asks before alerting anyone. ## Who it's for ✅ You use AI assistants every day and are tired of repeating yourself.
✅ You can't tell whether an assistant really finished the job.
✅ You want a person to say yes before an assistant touches money, customers or production.
✅ You want recurring work done without watching over it. ## Try it in five minutes ### On your computer, no account You need Git, Bun, and Node.js 22+ (real Node, not a Bun shim). No account or cloud credentials are needed. ```sh git clone https://github.com/tedix-hq/tedix.git && cd tedix bun run-local --demo ``` The launcher starts the API, database, and web app and prints `Tedix OS: http://localhost:3030`. Open it to look around a fictional company with a sample Deck and Feed. Run `bun run-local` without `--demo` to name your own local organization instead; Tedix creates it, your owner account, and a first tedi. Data stays on your machine in `.wrangler/run-local` (`.wrangler/run-local-demo` for the demo). Local mode makes no model calls by default, so tedis can't write anything yet. To turn on model calls through Workers AI on your own paid Cloudflare account: ```sh bunx wrangler login && bunx wrangler whoami # note your account id bun run-local --inference --workers-ai-account= ``` `--smoke` checks onboarding and exits. See [Getting started](docs/public/getting-started.md) for every option. ### In the assistant you already use (invited beta) Tedix Cloud is the hosted service. Ask for access through the [contact page](https://tedix.dev/contact/). With access: - **Claude, ChatGPT or Codex:** follow [Use Tedix in ChatGPT, Codex and Claude](docs/public/learning-paths/first-plugin.md). Claude chat and Cowork need no install, only a connector URL. - **From a terminal, with the CLI:** ```sh curl -fsSL https://downloads.tedix.dev/install.sh | sh tedix login ``` Then follow [Connect to Tedix Cloud](docs/public/learning-paths/first-connection.md). ## Available today, and what is not | Available today | Not yet | | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | The full source, which you can read and run on a computer. | Open sign-up for Tedix Cloud. Access is by invitation. | | Tedix Cloud, as an invited beta. | ChatGPT on the web. The ChatGPT desktop app works. | | The plugin for Claude, Codex and the ChatGPT desktop app. | Supported self-hosting. Running your own copy is experimental. | | The `tedix` command-line tool, as a public beta. | | [Release status](docs/public/release-status.md) has the details and the known limits. ## Words we use | Word | In plain words | | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Tedi** | An AI assistant with one job, its own memory and only the access you give it. | | **Home** | The chat where you ask for something. Tedix answers or hands it to a tedi. | | **Work** | Everything your team has handed off. One piece of it is a **Work Item**. | | **Deck** | The short stack of decisions waiting for you, one card at a time. | | **Feed** | A timeline of everything that happened, each entry with its record. | | **Run** | The saved record of one piece of work: what was used, what came out, who said yes. | | **Workspace** | A shared place for one area of work, with its documents, sheets and chats. | [Core concepts](docs/public/concepts.md) has the full list. ## For developers - Tedix connects to Claude (chat, Cowork and Claude Code), ChatGPT Work and Codex through the [Tedix plugin](plugins/tedix/README.md). Other clients that speak MCP, the open standard AI assistants use to call tools, connect through the [MCP gateway](docs/public/mcp-app-platform.md). - Any agent that reads Agent Skills can add Tedix's skills with `npx skills add tedix-hq/tedix-plugins`. - It runs on Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, Workflows, D1, and R2. - This repository is the whole product and the source Tedix Cloud is built from. The [documentation home](docs/public/index.md) lists every guide. - Give your coding agent [AGENT-REVIEW.md](AGENT-REVIEW.md) to evaluate Tedix for your project in about 15 minutes and send feedback without installing the CLI. ## Community, contributing and security Tedix is built by coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Devin and others) that Tedix itself coordinates, around the clock. Every commit names its Work Item and agent session in its trailers, so the history shows Tedix building Tedix. Your agent can contribute too: have it open an issue with a diff against current `main`, or follow [AGENT-REVIEW.md](AGENT-REVIEW.md) to send feedback in one step. Our agents re-author accepted fixes and credit you ([Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md#send-a-fix-from-your-coding-agent)). Ask questions and share what you build in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/tedix-hq/tedix/discussions). Report vulnerabilities through [Security](SECURITY.md). See also [Trademarks](TRADEMARKS.md). The CLI sends no telemetry; see [Telemetry and network contact](docs/public/telemetry.md). ## News - **2026-10-07**: The Tedix plugin restarted at version 0.1.0 and is now versioned independently of the CLI. - **2026-10-06**: The source is public on GitHub, with the first source prerelease, [v0.1.0-beta.1](https://github.com/tedix-hq/tedix/releases/tag/v0.1.0-beta.1). ## License Mostly AGPL-3.0; some packages are Apache-2.0 or MIT. sampled_files.README.md:
Tedix

Website · Docs · Discussions

**Hand off the work. Tedix brings back only the decisions that need you, and handles the rest.** ## The problem If you use AI assistants for real work, this probably sounds familiar: - You explain your company again in every new chat, to every tool. - An assistant says "done", and you can't see what it actually did. - You copy results by hand from one assistant to another. - Requests for your OK are spread across many open chats, so you keep checking on them. - Two people, or two assistants, end up doing the same job. ## What Tedix does - **One shared list of work.** People and assistants work from the same list, so everyone sees who owns what and nothing is done twice. - **Context that follows you.** Your company's facts, your preferences and past decisions reach whichever assistant you use: Claude, ChatGPT, Codex or Tedix's own. - **A record of every step.** Each piece of work keeps what was used, what came out and who said yes. - **Decisions one card at a time.** What needs you waits in one short stack, the Deck. Clear it on your phone or at your desk. Everything else goes to a timeline, the Feed, that you read when you want to. - **It stays yours.** Your goals, your decisions and what your team taught the assistants belong to your organization, even when you change models or tools. Tedix's own assistants are called **tedis**. A tedi has one job, its own memory and only the access you give it. It asks before anything risky, and nobody can approve their own request. ![A supplier folder in a Tedix OS workspace](docs/public/assets/tedix-os-supplier-review.png) _A tedi reviews one supplier folder, writes a decision note that cites its sources, and asks before sending anything. Run the small version in [examples/supplier-review](examples/supplier-review)._ ## Examples of recurring jobs - **Find conversations worth joining.** A tedi looks for public threads, for example on Reddit, where your product could help, and drafts a reply. You get one card per thread: post it, edit it or skip it. - **Match invoices against stock.** A tedi compares supplier invoices with what actually arrived and shows you only the mismatches. - **Act on critical error reports.** A tedi summarizes a new error report, finds who owns the problem and asks before alerting anyone. ## Who it's for ✅ You use AI assistants every day and are tired of repeating yourself.
✅ You can't tell whether an assistant really finished the job.
✅ You want a person to say yes before an assistant touches money, customers or production.
✅ You want recurring work done without watching over it. ## Try it in five minutes ### On your computer, no account You need Git, Bun, and Node.js 22+ (real Node, not a Bun shim). No account or cloud credentials are needed. ```sh git clone https://github.com/tedix-hq/tedix.git && cd tedix bun run-local --demo ``` The launcher starts the API, database, and web app and prints `Tedix OS: http://localhost:3030`. Open it to look around a fictional company with a sample Deck and Feed. Run `bun run-local` without `--demo` to name your own local organization instead; Tedix creates it, your owner account, and a first tedi. Data stays on your machine in `.wrangler/run-local` (`.wrangler/run-local-demo` for the demo). Local mode makes no model calls by default, so tedis can't write anything yet. To turn on model calls through Workers AI on your own paid Cloudflare account: ```sh bunx wrangler login && bunx wrangler whoami # note your account id bun run-local --inference --workers-ai-account= ``` `--smoke` checks onboarding and exits. See [Getting started](docs/public/getting-started.md) for every option. ### In the assistant you already use (invited beta) Tedix Cloud is the hosted service. Ask for access through the [contact page](https://tedix.dev/contact/). With access: - **Claude, ChatGPT or Codex:** follow [Use Tedix in ChatGPT, Codex and Claude](docs/public/learning-paths/first-plugin.md). Claude chat and Cowork need no install, only a connector URL. - **From a terminal, with the CLI:** ```sh curl -fsSL https://downloads.tedix.dev/install.sh | sh tedix login ``` Then follow [Connect to Tedix Cloud](docs/public/learning-paths/first-connection.md). ## Available today, and what is not | Available today | Not yet | | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | The full source, which you can read and run on a computer. | Open sign-up for Tedix Cloud. Access is by invitation. | | Tedix Cloud, as an invited beta. | ChatGPT on the web. The ChatGPT desktop app works. | | The plugin for Claude, Codex and the ChatGPT desktop app. | Supported self-hosting. Running your own copy is experimental. | | The `tedix` command-line tool, as a public beta. | | [Release status](docs/public/release-status.md) has the details and the known limits. ## Words we use | Word | In plain words | | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Tedi** | An AI assistant with one job, its own memory and only the access you give it. | | **Home** | The chat where you ask for something. Tedix answers or hands it to a tedi. | | **Work** | Everything your team has handed off. One piece of it is a **Work Item**. | | **Deck** | The short stack of decisions waiting for you, one card at a time. | | **Feed** | A timeline of everything that happened, each entry with its record. | | **Run** | The saved record of one piece of work: what was used, what came out, who said yes. | | **Workspace** | A shared place for one area of work, with its documents, sheets and chats. | [Core concepts](docs/public/concepts.md) has the full list. ## For developers - Tedix connects to Claude (chat, Cowork and Claude Code), ChatGPT Work and Codex through the [Tedix plugin](plugins/tedix/README.md). Other clients that speak MCP, the open standard AI assistants use to call tools, connect through the [MCP gateway](docs/public/mcp-app-platform.md). - Any agent that reads Agent Skills can add Tedix's skills with `npx skills add tedix-hq/tedix-plugins`. - It runs on Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, Workflows, D1, and R2. - This repository is the whole product and the source Tedix Cloud is built from. The [documentation home](docs/public/index.md) lists every guide. - Give your coding agent [AGENT-REVIEW.md](AGENT-REVIEW.md) to evaluate Tedix for your project in about 15 minutes and send feedback without installing the CLI. ## Community, contributing and security Tedix is built by coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Devin and others) that Tedix itself coordinates, around the clock. Every commit names its Work Item and agent session in its trailers, so the history shows Tedix building Tedix. Your agent can contribute too: have it open an issue with a diff against current `main`, or follow [AGENT-REVIEW.md](AGENT-REVIEW.md) to send feedback in one step. Our agents re-author accepted fixes and credit you ([Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md#send-a-fix-from-your-coding-agent)). Ask questions and share what you build in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/tedix-hq/tedix/discussions). Report vulnerabilities through [Security](SECURITY.md). See also [Trademarks](TRADEMARKS.md). The CLI sends no telemetry; see [Telemetry and network contact](docs/public/telemetry.md). ## News - **2026-10-07**: The Tedix plugin restarted at version 0.1.0 and is now versioned independently of the CLI. - **2026-10-06**: The source is public on GitHub, with the first source prerelease, [v0.1.0-beta.1](https://github.com/tedix-hq/tedix/releases/tag/v0.1.0-beta.1). ## License Mostly AGPL-3.0; some packages are Apache-2.0 or MIT. See [Licensing](docs/public/licensing.md) and [Third-Party Notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

repository.readme:
# LLMSlim **Long-term memory and context selection for AI agents and coding tools, with no LLM call.** LLMSlim stores what users and agents say word for word, then returns the parts that answer a question within a token budget you set. It runs as an MCP server, a Python library or a small HTTP server. [![PyPI Version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/llmslim.svg?style=flat-square&logo=pypi&logoColor=white&color=38bdf8)](https://pypi.org/project/llmslim/) [![PyPI Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/personalized-badge/llmslim?period=total&units=INTERNATIONAL_SYSTEM&left_color=BLACK&right_color=ORANGE&left_text=downloads)](https://pepy.tech/projects/llmslim) [![MCP Registry: io.github.Thanatos9404/llmslim](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP_Registry-io.github.Thanatos9404%2Fllmslim-0098FF?style=flat-square)](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=io.github.Thanatos9404/llmslim) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-94a3b8?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![llmslim MCP server: quality and maintenance score on Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Thanatos9404/llmslim/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Thanatos9404/llmslim) [**Examples**](examples/) • [**Documentation**](https://www.llmslim.app/docs) • [**Live Studio Playground**](https://www.llmslim.app) • [**Sarvam Integration**](https://www.llmslim.app/integrations/sarvam) • [**Benchmarks**](#-benchmarks--radical-transparency) • [**Changelog**](CHANGELOG.md) A real Python session with llmslim 0.11.1 from PyPI, typed by a script and recorded with asciinema (script, recording).
## Use it in 30 seconds Each MCP setup below starts the same server, `llmslim mcp`, with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (Python 3.10 or newer). Memory goes to a local SQLite file, `~/.llmslim/memory.db`. **One click:** [![Install in VS Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/VS_Code-Install_Server-0098FF?style=flat-square&logo=visualstudiocode&logoColor=white)](https://vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=llmslim&config=%7B%22command%22%3A%22uvx%22%2C%22args%22%3A%5B%22--from%22%2C%22llmslim%5Bmcp%5D%3D%3D0.11.1%22%2C%22llmslim%22%2C%22mcp%22%5D%7D) [![Add to Cursor](https://cursor.com/deeplink/mcp-install-dark.svg)](https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=llmslim&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoidXZ4IiwiYXJncyI6WyItLWZyb20iLCJsbG1zbGltW21jcF09PTAuMTEuMSIsImxsbXNsaW0iLCJtY3AiXX0%3D) [![Add to LM Studio](https://files.lmstudio.ai/deeplink/mcp-install-dark.svg)](https://lmstudio.ai/install-mcp?name=llmslim&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoidXZ4IiwiYXJncyI6WyItLWZyb20iLCJsbG1zbGltW21jcF09PTAuMTEuMSIsImxsbXNsaW0iLCJtY3AiXX0%3D) [![Install in Goose](https://goose-docs.ai/img/extension-install-dark.svg)](https://goose-docs.ai/extension?cmd=uvx&arg=--from&arg=llmslim%5Bmcp%5D%3D%3D0.11.1&arg=llmslim&arg=mcp&id=llmslim&name=LLMSlim&description=Long-term%20memory%20for%20agents%20with%20no%20LLM%20in%20the%20loop) [![Add to Kiro](https://kiro.dev/images/add-to-kiro.svg)](https://kiro.dev/launch/mcp/add?name=llmslim&config=%7B%22command%22%3A%22uvx%22%2C%22args%22%3A%5B%22--from%22%2C%22llmslim%5Bmcp%5D%3D%3D0.11.1%22%2C%22llmslim%22%2C%22mcp%22%5D%7D) | Tool | Run | | :--- | :--- | | Claude Code | `claude mcp add llmslim -- uvx --from "llmslim[mcp]" llmslim mcp` | | Claude Code plugin | `/plugin marketplace add Thanatos9404/llmslim`, then `/plugin install llmslim@llmslim` | | Codex | `codex mcp add llmslim -- uvx --from "llmslim[mcp]" llmslim mcp` | | GitHub Copilot CLI | `copilot mcp add llmslim -- uvx --from "llmslim[mcp]" llmslim mcp` | | Gemini CLI | `gemini extensions install https://github.com/Thanatos9404/llmslim` | | Hermes Agent | `hermes plugins install llmslim --enable`, then `hermes config set context.engine llmslim`: a context engine that compacts long conversations locally ([plugin](plugins/hermes/README.md)) | The first start downloads LLMSlim and its dependencies. If a client gives up waiting, run `uvx --from "llmslim[mcp]" llmslim mcp --help` once to fill uv's cache, then restart the client. **Python** (`pip install llmslim`, Python 3.9 or newer): ```python from llmslim.memory import Memory mem = Memory("memory.db") # a SQLite file; Memory("postgresql://...") with llmslim[postgres] mem.add([{"role": "user", "content": "I'm allergic to peanuts."}], user_id="asha") context = mem.search("Am I allergic to anything?", user_id="asha", budget=1500) print(context.text) # put it in your prompt as data, not instructions ``` **TypeScript** (`npm install llmslim`, Node 18 or newer), against `llmslim serve` (`pip install "llmslim[server]"`): ```ts import { LLMSlim } from "llmslim"; const slim = new LLMSlim(); // http://127.0.0.1:8080 unless LLMSLIM_BASE_URL is set await slim.memories.add({ userId: "asha", messages: "I'm allergic to peanuts." }); const context = await slim.memories.search({ userId: "asha", query: "Am I allergic to anything?", budget: 1500 }); ``` Runnable examples, each with a test: [Claude Code memory](examples/claude-code-memory/), [LangChain agent](examples/langchain-agent-memory/), [Pydantic AI agent](examples/pydantic-ai-memory/), [big logs](examples/fit-context-big-logs/) and [TypeScript](examples/typescript-client/). If LLMSlim is useful, a star helps others find it. Feedback is welcome in [issues](https://github.com/Thanatos9404/llmslim/issues). ## What it does - **Five MCP tools:** `remember`, `recall`, `list_memories`, `forget` and `fit_context`. - **Stores messages word for word** in SQLite or Postgres. Nothing is summarized or extracted on the way in. - **Recalls within a token budget.** `recall` returns the stored messages that answer a question, under their dates and whole where they fit, within the budget you set. `fit_context` shrinks a long log or document to a budget. - **Fixes the scope at server start.** The user and agent ids are set when the server starts, not by the model, so a model steered by injected text can't read or delete another user's memory. - **Makes no LLM call.** By default, storing and recalling are plain code: no model, no embedding API, no API key. - **MIT licensed.** The library needs Python 3.9 or newer, the MCP server 3.10 or newer. Beyond memory, LLMSlim Core also compresses and plans prompts, chat history, retrieved documents and tool schemas into token budgets: see the sections below. ### Why no LLM call Storing is a database write and recall is deterministic ranking code. So what comes back is what was said, not a model's rewrite of it, and the same history and question always give the same context, which makes recall easy to test. The memory server and `llmslim serve` make no network calls of their own. What does reach the network: installing from PyPI (including `uvx`'s first run of a version) and tiktoken downloading its tokenizer file once. The trade-off: the default lexical mode matches words, not meanings, so a question phrased differently from the stored message can miss it. `relevance="semantic"` adds an optional cross-encoder for that (`llmslim[semantic]`, which downloads the model the first time). See the [limits](docs/MEMORY.md#limits). --- ## Compress a prompt in 60 seconds **1. Install** LLMSlim Core from PyPI (Python 3.9+). LLMSlim Holographic Engine: Multi-stage token compression condensing sparse context streams into dense information cores with zero contract mutation.

Modern LLM systems suffer from the **Context Window Dilemma**: 1. **Financial Tax**: Re-sending large prompts on every turn means you pay for the same input tokens again and again. 2. **Latency Bottleneck**: Large prompts inflate Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) and queue times. 3. **Lost-In-The-Middle Syndrome**: Models can miss or misuse information buried in the middle of long contexts. 4. **Security Risks**: Untrusted RAG content can smuggle indirect prompt injections into system instructions. **LLMSlim fixes this at the source.** It provides deterministic, contract-preserving compression that runs natively in your application layer before calling any model. ### 💎 Core Architectural Pillars | Pillar | How LLMSlim Solves It | | :--- | :--- | | **🏎️ Ultra-Low Overhead** | Pure Python + NumPy/Scikit-learn. Median **0.026 ms** per sample (p95 1.889 ms) in the 24-sample, mostly short-text [Phase 2 evaluation](benchmarks/reports/latest.md), with no model calls on the default path. Longer inputs take longer. | | **🔒 Deterministic by Default** | The default extractive mode only selects sentences from your input, so output is reproducible and contains no generated text. It can still drop a fact you need, so check results for your use case. Rewrite and hybrid modes call your own LLM. | | **🛡️ Provenance Security** | `ContextRole` hierarchy isolates untrusted RAG/tool text so prompt injections cannot escalate to `system` priority. | | **🧩 Contract-Safe Tool Schemas** | Canonical JSON normalization, SHA-256 contract fingerprints, and zero execution rewrites for agent tooling. | | **🔌 Provider-Neutral** | Execution-free request builders for Sarvam, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and vLLM, plus an OpenAI Agents SDK bridge. Works with any framework that can pass plain message or document lists. | --- ## 🖥️ Live Studio Playground ([www.llmslim.app](https://www.llmslim.app)) Paste a long chat, a stack of search results or a CI log, ask a question, and watch LLMSlim keep what answers it. No provider SDK, PyTorch, sentence-transformers, or cloud service is required for the default installation.* --- ## ⚡ Quick Start & Usage Patterns ### 1. Basic Extractive Compression (Default) ```python from llmslim import ContextRole, compress text = """ The Apollo program was conceived in 1960 during the Eisenhower administration. NASA announced the program as a follow-up to Project Mercury. The spacecraft was designed to carry three astronauts. Apollo succeeded in landing the first humans on the Moon in 1969. Funding for the program peaked in 1966 with over $4.5 billion appropriated. """ result = compress( text, target_ratio=0.5, # Target: keep about 50% of the tokens strategy="extractive", # Deterministic sentence selection context_role=ContextRole.GENERAL, ) print("Compressed Output:") print(result.compressed_text) print(f"Original: {result.original_tokens} tokens | Compressed: {result.compressed_tokens} tokens") print(f"Saved: {result.tokens_saved} tokens ({result.reduction_percent:.1f}%)") print(f"Sentences kept: {result.sentences_kept} of {result.sentences_total}") ``` Extractive selection keeps whole sentences, not meaning: always check that the sentences you need survived. On this text, the 0.7.1 base install keeps three of the five sentences and drops the 1969 Moon landing sentence; with `llmslim[fast-tokens]` (tiktoken counts) it keeps that sentence and drops another. --- ### 2. Multi-Document RAG Compression Compress each retrieved chunk before you build the prompt. `compress_documents` takes plain strings and returns one result per document, in order: ```python from llmslim import compress_documents documents = [ "Q3 revenue grew 23% year-over-year to $1.2B. " "Growth came mainly from enterprise subscriptions in India and Southeast Asia. " "The board met twice during the quarter. " "The office cafeteria menu was updated in August. " "A new logo was unveiled at the annual offsite. " "Net revenue retention reached 118%, up from 109% a year earlier.", "Operating expenses rose 11% because of AI research infrastructure. " "Most of the increase was GPU capacity for model evaluation. " "Travel costs were flat. " "The parking garage was repainted in September. " "Employees voted on a new name for the meeting rooms. " "Headcount in engineering grew by 40 people.", ] results = compress_documents( documents, query="What drove Q3 revenue and cost changes?", target_ratio=0.5, ) context = "\n\n".join(r.compressed_text for r in results) print(context) print(f"Saved {sum(r.tokens_saved for r in results)} tokens across {len(results)} documents") ``` With a query, the documents share one budget and it goes where the query points. Relevance is lexical by default (BM25 with feedback: no model, deterministic, tens of milliseconds on a 3k-token context). For RAG and long chat memory, where the answer often shares few words with the question, add the optional reranker: ```python # pip install "llmslim[semantic]" (sentence-transformers; uses a GPU when there is one) results = compress_documents(documents, query=question, target_ratio=0.25, relevance="semantic") ``` `relevance` also accepts any callable `scorer(query, texts) -> scores`, such as a hosted reranking API. Retrieving with LangChain, LlamaIndex or Haystack? Use the [framework adapters](#use-with-langchain--llamaindex--haystack) instead of calling `compress_documents` yourself. > [!NOTE] > `compress_documents` treats documents as untrusted (`ContextRole.RAG`) by default, > so imperative wording inside a retrieved document is never force-kept as a > protected instruction. It does **not** remove injected text: an injected sentence > can still survive compression. To mark retrieved content as untrusted in the final > prompt, use [`plan_context`](#adaptive-context-planner-v060) or > [`ContextRuntime`](#agent-context-runtime-v070), which wrap every document in a > `trusted="false"` provenance tag and ignore any role a document claims for itself. --- ### 3. Multi-Turn Chat Conversation Compression Compress long earlier turns while passing `system` instructions and user questions through unchanged: ```python from llmslim import compress_chat_messages review = ( "Here are my suggestions for your schema. First, add a composite index on " "(customer_id, created_at) because most of your queries filter by customer and sort by " "date. Second, the orders table stores the shipping address inline, which duplicates " "data across rows; move it to an addresses table. Third, the status column is a " "free-text string, so use an enum or a lookup table instead. Fourth, the price column " "uses FLOAT, which loses precision for money; use DECIMAL(12, 2). Finally, add ON " "DELETE RESTRICT to the foreign key from orders to customers so that deleting a " "customer cannot silently orphan their orders." ) messages = [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a specialized code review engineer."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Can you review my database schema design?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": review}, {"role": "user", "content": "What about the foreign key constraint on line 42?"}, ] compressed_messages = compress_chat_messages( messages, target_ratio=0.5, compressible_roles=("assistant",), # Only compress assistant turns; system and user pass through min_tokens=60, # Turns shorter than this are never compressed ) for message in compressed_messages: print(f"{message['role']}: {message['content']}") ``` --- ### 4. Hybrid Prompt Optimization (Extractive + Rewrite) Combine ultra-fast extractive pre-filtering with your own LLM provider for deep semantic paraphrasing: ```python from llmslim import CallableProvider, compress import openai client = openai.OpenAI() # reads OPENAI_API_KEY; requires `pip install openai` long_raw_text = """ The Apollo program was conceived in 1960 during the Eisenhower administration. NASA announced the program as a follow-up to Project Mercury. The spacecraft was designed to carry three astronauts. Apollo succeeded in landing the first humans on the Moon in 1969. Funding for the program peaked in 1966 with over $4.5 billion appropriated. """ # Define your own provider callback (LLMSlim does not bundle vendor SDKs). # The callback receives a RewriteRequest with ready-made prompts and returns text. provider = CallableProvider( lambda req: client.chat.completions.create( model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=[ {"role": "system", "content": req.system_prompt}, {"role": "user", "content": req.user_prompt}, ], ).choices[0].message.content ) result = compress( long_raw_text, target_ratio=0.3, strategy="hybrid", # 1. Extractive filter -> 2. LLM semantic rewrite provider=provider, ) meta = result.rewrite_metadata print(result.compressed_text) print(f"Strategy: {meta.strategy} | Rewrite accepted: {meta.accepted} | Fell back to extractive: {meta.fallback_used}") print("Validation failures:", meta.failure_reasons) ``` Every rewrite is validated for structure, instruction retention, entity retention, and similarity. If a hybrid rewrite fails validation, LLMSlim returns the extractive result instead and reports why in `rewrite_metadata.failure_reasons`. --- ## Coding agents: `llmslim wrap claude` Claude Code resends the whole conversation on every turn. So long test logs, build output, search results and web pages get paid for again and again, and they add to the context that Claude Code eventually compacts. `llmslim wrap claude` runs Claude Code through a local proxy: - It shrinks such output the first time the model sees it. Lines that look like errors, failures or warnings come first, then the lines related to the command. - It sends exactly the same bytes on every later request, so the prompt cache keeps hitting and Claude's thinking stays valid. - Output of Claude Code's own `Read`, `Edit` and `Write` tools is never touched. A file printed through the shell (`cat`, `head`) counts as shell output. ```bash pip install "llmslim[proxy]" llmslim wrap claude llmslim proxy stats ``` **What it does to the bill, measured** on real Claude Code 2.1.296 with Claude Haiku 5.5, on eight small synthetic tasks. We counted list-price dollars from the API's usage, with cache reads priced separately, and published all 572 runs in [benchmarks/claude_code_cost](benchmarks/claude_code_cost/README.md). The primary result has both arms in Claude Code's default permission mode; a second run has both in auto mode. - **Long logs:** a simulated failing CI run (about 12 KB of log, the cause in the middle) cost 26-32% less, and a lint run with three errors among 240 warnings 17-21% less. - **Test runs:** about 4% less in default mode, within noise for every task; 2-15% less in auto mode. Agents already trim test output with `tail`. - **Over 8 tasks:** +5.3% in default mode (95% interval +1.5% to +9.4%), mostly from one task where shortened JSON cost about twice as much; -5.1% in auto mode. JSON is left alone by default since 0.11.1. - **Real sessions:** in an offline replay of the maintainer's own transcripts (32 sessions and the 412 subagent runs they started, almost all Claude Opus 5.5, at list prices), tool output was a small part of the bill: with the same turns, all shell, search and web output costing nothing would have cut it by 13.4%. Re-reading long context was the big part. Claude Code's `/autocompact` setting decides when it compacts; what that does to cost is not measured here. Without the byte-for-byte replay, an edited history invalidates Claude's thinking: in our API check on Claude Haiku 5.5 the request was rejected with HTTP 400, the default for accounts created on or after 31 August 2026. With the replay, cache reads grew on every request of a 7-request API test. See [docs/PROXY.md](docs/PROXY.md) for what is compressed, the limits and security. **As a Claude Code plugin.** The plugin adds LLMSlim's memory server (below) and two commands: - `/llmslim:wrap-claude` walks you through starting Claude Code through the proxy; - `/llmslim:savings` shows how many tool-output tokens the proxy kept out of your requests: an estimate counted before prompt-cache discounts, not dollars saved. ```text /plugin marketplace add Thanatos9404/llmslim /plugin install llmslim@llmslim ``` On Claude Code 2.1.275 or later, `/plugin install llmslim --marketplace Thanatos9404/llmslim` does both in one step. The memory server runs with `uvx`, so it needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). ## Memory for agents, with no LLM in the loop `llmslim.memory` stores every turn verbatim and selects, at read time, the turns that answer a question within a token budget. There is no extraction model on the way in and no model call on the way out. ```python from llmslim.memory import Memory memory = Memory("memory.db") # SQLite, built into Python memory.add([{"role": "user", "content": "I'm allergic to peanuts."}], user_id="asha") context = memory.search("Am I allergic to anything?", user_id="asha", budget=1500) print(context.text) # put it in the prompt as untrusted data ``` It runs the pipeline behind the round-3 benchmarks. On Mem0's own LongMemEval questions, that pipeline (with its reranker) answered 78.3% for $1.04 per 1,000 questions, against 76.7% for $220.88 for Mem0. Coming from Mem0? `from llmslim.memory.compat import Mem0Memory as Memory` keeps Mem0's method names. See [docs/MEMORY.md](docs/MEMORY.md) for scopes, stores, evidence and limits, and the [1.0 roadmap](docs/roadmap/1.0.md). ### In Claude, Cursor or any MCP client `llmslim mcp` serves this memory over MCP, with a `fit_context` tool for long text. The routes, limits and Docker setup are in [docs/SERVER.md](docs/SERVER.md). The TypeScript client, `npm install llmslim` ([clients/typescript](clients/typescript)), wraps this API with no dependencies. It also gives the Vercel AI SDK `recall_memory` and `remember` tools and a middleware that saves turns. None of them changes your prompt, so prompt caches keep hitting and Claude's preserved thinking stays valid. ## Use with LangChain / LlamaIndex / Haystack Each adapter runs `compress_documents` on the retrieved documents, with the same shared budget when there is a query. Kept documents keep their metadata, and documents that compress to nothing are dropped. They run locally with no model. | Framework | Install | Class | Use it where you'd use | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | LangChain | `llmslim[langchain]` | `llmslim.integrations.langchain.LLMSlimCompressor` | `LLMLinguaCompressor`, e.g. in `ContextualCompressionRetriever` | | LlamaIndex | `llmslim[llamaindex]` (Python 3.10+) | `llmslim.integrations.llama_index.LLMSlimPostprocessor` | `LongLLMLinguaPostprocessor`, in `node_postprocessors` | | Haystack | `llmslim[haystack]` | `llmslim.integrations.haystack.LLMSlimDocumentCompressor` | a component between the retriever and the prompt builder | ```python from langchain_classic.retrievers.contextual_compression import ContextualCompressionRetriever from llmslim.integrations.langchain import LLMSlimCompressor retriever = ContextualCompressionRetriever( base_compressor=LLMSlimCompressor(target_ratio=0.25), base_retriever=your_retriever, ) ``` Runnable examples with their output: [LangChain](https://github.com/Thanatos9404/llmslim/blob/main/docs/integrations/LANGCHAIN.md), [LlamaIndex](https://github.com/Thanatos9404/llmslim/blob/main/docs/integrations/LLAMAINDEX.md), [Haystack](https://github.com/Thanatos9404/llmslim/blob/main/docs/integrations/HAYSTACK.md). --- ## Use with gptme / Hermes Agent / Pydantic AI These adapters fit an agent's message history into a token budget. They keep the system prompt, tool calls and the latest turns as they are, compress older tool output and turns locally (failures and tracebacks in tool output are kept), and keep every tool call paired with its result. There is no model call. | Agent | Install | Class or function | How it plugs in | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | gptme | `llmslim[gptme]` (gptme 0.34+) | `llmslim.integrations.gptme.LLMSlimContextProvider` | gptme context provider `llmslim`; `[plugin.llmslim] compaction = true` makes it the one gptme's compaction uses | | Hermes Agent | llmslim in Hermes's environment | `llmslim.integrations.hermes.LLMSlimContextEngine` | `ContextEngine` plugin `llmslim`; select it with `context.engine: llmslim` | | Pydantic AI | `llmslim[pydantic-ai]` (1.0+) | `llmslim.integrations.pydantic_ai.llmslim_history_processor` | history processor, in `ProcessHistory(...)` or `history_processors=[...]` | ```python from pydantic_ai import Agent from pydantic_ai.capabilities import ProcessHistory from llmslim.integrations.pydantic_ai import llmslim_history_processor agent = Agent( "openai:gpt-5", capabilities=[ProcessHistory(llmslim_history_processor(max_tokens=8_000))], ) ``` Setup and runnable examples with their output: [gptme](https://github.com/Thanatos9404/llmslim/blob/main/docs/integrations/GPTME.md), [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/Thanatos9404/llmslim/blob/main/docs/integrations/HERMES.md), [Pydantic AI](https://github.com/Thanatos9404/llmslim/blob/main/docs/integrations/PYDANTIC_AI.md). --- ## 🛡️ Security Architecture: Provenance Isolation Compression algorithms that naively score sentences based on imperative keywords (`"Must"`, `"Always"`, `"Action Required"`) introduce a severe vulnerability: **indirect prompt injection amplification**. An attacker injecting malicious instructions into a retrieved RAG document can trick the compressor into preserving the attack payload while discarding legitimate context. We found this issue in LLMSlim internally and fixed it in v0.3.1. No CVE or security advisory was published, and the issue has no official CVSS score. LLMSlim solves this via an explicit **Context Role Trust Boundary**: ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ HIGHEST TRUST (Priority Tier 4) │ │ System & Developer Prompts (Strictly Protected) │ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ INTERMEDIATE TRUST (Priority Tier 2-3) │ │ Direct User Input │ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ PROVENANCE-LOCKED (Priority Tier 0-1) │ │ RAG Documents • Assistant History • Tool Outputs │ │ *Cannot reach Tier 4 through imperative patterns* │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` 1. **Hardened Priority Locking**: Content marked `ContextRole.RAG`, `ContextRole.TOOL`, or `ContextRole.ASSISTANT` cannot achieve Tier-4 priority, regardless of imperative syntax. 2. **Nonce-Protected Rewrite Delimiters**: When the input contains a fence-like token such as `---END TEXT---`, the rewrite template's fences get a random per-call nonce, so the embedded token cannot close the text region. The input itself is never modified. 3. **Untrusted by default, not filtered**: these protections stop injected text from gaining priority. They do not delete it. `plan_context` and `ContextRuntime` label it `trusted="false"` in the final context so your model and application can treat it accordingly. --- ## 🧩 Contract-Safe Tool Schemas & MCP Ingestion Large agent catalogs (dozens or hundreds of tool definitions) waste thousands of tokens before an agent even starts thinking. LLMSlim introduces **Contract-Safe Tool Infrastructure** (v0.4.0 & v0.5.0): ```python from llmslim.tools import ( canonical_json, contract_equivalent, fingerprint_tool_schema, from_mcp_tool, optimize_tool_schema, ) # 1. Ingest authoritative raw tool definition raw_tool = { "name": "enterprise.search_ledger", "description": "Searches financial transaction records by date range.", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": {"account_id": {"type": "string"}, "limit": {"type": "integer"}}, "required": ["account_id"], }, } # 2. Parse and safely optimize schema formatting tool = from_mcp_tool(raw_tool, namespace="finance") result = optimize_tool_schema(tool) # 3. Mathematically verify exact contract equivalence assert result.equivalence.status.value == "EXACT" assert fingerprint_tool_schema(tool) == fingerprint_tool_schema(result.optimized) print("Canonical Fingerprint:", fingerprint_tool_schema(result.optimized)) print(canonical_json(result.optimized.raw)) ``` ### Async MCP Catalog Source (v0.5.0) Requires `pip install "llmslim[mcp]"` (Python 3.10+) and an MCP server you run: ```python import asyncio from llmslim.mcp import MCPToolCatalogSource, PlanMode, plan_catalog_context async def main() -> None: # Streamable HTTP MCP source with bounded pagination and stale-cache detection source = MCPToolCatalogSource.from_streamable_http( "http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer local-token"}, ) snapshot = await source.list_tools() plan = plan_catalog_context(snapshot, mode=PlanMode.FULL) print(f"Catalog contains {len(snapshot.tools)} tools ({plan.metrics.catalog_tokens} tokens)") asyncio.run(main()) ``` --- ## 📊 Benchmarks & Radical Transparency Many libraries make unsubstantiated claims about 90% prompt compression. At LLMSlim, we practice **Radical Benchmark Transparency**: ### Round 3: Core 0.9.0 against memory systems and compressors, cost first Measured 13-15 October 2026 on held-out test questions. Every system is read by Claude Haiku 5.5 with the same answer prompt and judges. Mem0 and Zep ran through their own benchmark harnesses, and LLMLingua-2 and LongLLMLingua (LLaMA-2-7B in float16) with their published settings. Every compressor's context was built in public Kaggle notebooks pinned to a commit. Each cell is accuracy and what 1,000 questions cost end to end at list prices: the answer call, Mem0's and Zep's memory-building calls, and each system's compute. Full tables, confidence intervals, weak spots and every answer: [benchmarks/live/round3](benchmarks/live/round3/RESULTS.md). | Benchmark | LLMSlim 0.9 + reranker | LLMSlim 0.9 (no model) | Mem0 | Zep | LongLLMLingua | LLMLingua-2 | Retrieval baseline* | Full context | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | LoCoMo, 1,307 q, ~2,500 tokens | **93.0% · $0.95** | 91.7% · $0.89 | 91.0% · $2.66 | 74.4% · $6.24 | 73.3% · $7.01 (300 q) | 34.1% · $0.43 | 85.2% · $0.90 | 95.1% · $0.83 cached | | LongMemEval-S, 180 q, ~10,000 tokens | 74.4% · $2.21 | **77.8% · $2.13** | | | not run | 15.6% · $8.43 | 80.6% · $4.45 | 77.8% · $90.21 | | LongMemEval-S, Mem0's 60 q, ~2,500 tokens | **78.3% · $1.04** | 71.7% · $0.96 | 76.7% · $220.88 | | | | 80.0% · $3.36 | 78.3% · $90.20 | | LongMemEval-S, Zep's 24 q, ~2,500 tokens | 87.5% · $1.01 | **87.5% · $0.94** | 87.5% · $219.48 | 58.3% · $697.56 | | | 83.3% · $3.28 | 91.7% · $90.22 | | NaturalQuestions, 2,255 q, 25% of tokens | **73.5% · $0.33** | 60.6% · $0.30 | | | 70.5% · $1.32 (1,000 q) | 52.5% · $0.87 | 73.9% · $0.30 | 78.4% · $0.65 | | HotpotQA, 2,000 q, 40% of tokens (exact match) | 52.2% · $0.15 | **52.4% · $0.13** | | | 50.4% · $0.77 (1,000 q) | 46.7% · $0.47 | 50.5% · $0.13 | 58.0% · $0.24 | \* Dense retrieval over turns (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) on LoCoMo and LongMemEval; a plain reranker on NaturalQuestions and HotpotQA. Mem0 is its top 50 memories, except top 200 on Mem0's own sample. LongLLMLingua ran on pre-registered samples; on the same questions LLMSlim with its reranker scores 93.3% on LoCoMo (+20.0, 95% CI +15.0 to +25.0) and 72.7% on NaturalQuestions, and the default LLMSlim 53.3% on HotpotQA. A cached full history costs $4.48 per 1,000 LoCoMo questions when the cache misses. **Where LLMSlim loses:** - **NaturalQuestions without the reranker.** The default lexical mode scores 60.6% against 73.9% for a plain reranker: paraphrased questions need semantic matching, so use the reranker for open-domain retrieval. - **Dense retrieval on LongMemEval.** 80.6% to LLMSlim's 77.8% at 10,000 tokens and 76.1% to 74.4% at 2,500, at about twice the cost. Neither gap is significant on 180 questions, but both point the same way. A fix that narrowed it on development questions did not hold up on test, so it is not in 0.9.0. - **Multi-hop and temporal questions at 1,000 tokens.** Mem0's top 20 memories beat the default LLMSlim on LoCoMo's multi-hop (88.7% vs 80.3%) and temporal (93.4% vs 85.7%) questions. With its reranker LLMSlim is ahead overall (90.5% vs 88.7%). - **A cached full history.** When a conversation's questions come back to back, the cached history (95.1% for $0.83) beats every compressed context on LoCoMo. ### Long documents and agents: round 2, Core 0.8.0 Same model and prompt for every configuration; truncation gets exactly LLMSlim's token count, and every suite was rerun once on a fresh sample after the code was frozen ([benchmarks/live](benchmarks/live/README.md)). 0.9.0 changes only how plain-text chat transcripts are selected. | Benchmark | Full context | LLMSlim 0.8 + reranker | LLMSlim 0.8 (no model) | Truncate, same budget | Tokens (full → LLMSlim) | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | LongBench v1, 210 samples (macro) | 54.9 | 54.2 | **54.9** | 45.2 | 15,532 → 5,232 | | … fresh 210 samples | 55.1 | **55.4** | 55.0 | 46.8 | | | LongBench v2, 180 q (accuracy) | 60.0 | **55.6** | 53.9 | 48.3 | 30,493 → 8,469 | | SWE-bench Verified Mini, 50 issues (resolved) | 36-38 | not run | **38** | not run | 48-58k → 51k per task | The reranker is optional (`relevance="semantic"`, a 22M-parameter cross-encoder from the `semantic` extra); without it LLMSlim runs no model at all. > [!NOTE] > **The Schema-Tax Measurement**: In our v0.4.0 benchmark across 375 synthetic tool schemas in 18 catalogs written for this repository (see the [dataset card](docs/phase-2/DATASET_CARD.md)), lossless schema compression saved **0 tokens (0.00%)** when the baseline was already compact canonical JSON. We publish this result transparently: we never claim imaginary savings where none exist. ### v0.6 Adaptive Planner (Frozen Offline Suite) | Method | Budget success | Context reduction | Required facts | Hard constraints | Mean latency* | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **Raw full context** | 71.4% | 0.0% | 100% | 100% | measurement only | | **Naive prefix** | 100% | 9.2% | 100% | 100% | 2.21 ms | | **Fixed-ratio compressor** | 78.6% | 9.6% | 94.0% | 96.4% | 26.55 ms | | **Adaptive planner** | **96.4%** | **11.4%** | **100%** | **100%** | 208.02 ms | The 28-case corpus covers chat, RAG, tools, mixed, external-source, and 12-language multilingual cases. The sole adaptive infeasibility is an intentionally impossible full-catalog case; it is reported explicitly. These task-grounded checks are not an LLM-judge or universal quality claim. *Latency is specific to the checked-in run and hardware. See the [release gate results](docs/releases/v0.6.0-RELEASE_GATE.md#frozen-benchmark-result), [raw results](benchmarks/results/v0.6-planner-latest.json), and frozen [dataset](benchmarks/datasets/v06_context_planning.json).* The live Sarvam harness was not run without both explicit opt-in and credentials. --- ## 🖥️ Command-Line Interface (CLI) Compress files, streams, or prompts directly from your terminal: ```bash # Compress a document to 50% ratio llmslim document.txt -o compressed.txt --ratio 0.5 # Pipeline integration with jq / curl cat input.txt | llmslim --ratio 0.4 --mode rag > rag_context.txt # Inspect token count differences llmslim document.txt --stats ``` --- ## 📋 Changelog Release notes for every version, including 0.11.1, are in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Thanatos9404/llmslim/releases). --- ## 🤝 Ecosystem Integrations LLMSlim operates as an unopinionated context pre-processor. These integrations ship in Core; none of them sends a request for you. Every integration that spends a vendor credit is checked by a `UsageGuard` before the request leaves the process (per-minute rate, lifetime request cap and a unit cap in INR, USD or queries, configurable with `LLMSLIM__*` variables; see `.env.example`):
| Provider / Framework | What ships in Core | Pattern | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Sarvam AI** | `llmslim[sarvam]`: `SarvamProvider`/`AsyncSarvamProvider`, `SarvamLanguageTools`, `SarvamDocumentSource`, `annotate_languages()`/`normalize_scripts()`, `sarvam_messages()` | Local planning + official `sarvamai` Python SDK, guarded with dated INR prices | | **Exa** | `llmslim[exa]`: `ExaSearchSource`, vendor-neutral `WebSearchSource` | Untrusted RAG context items with URL, date and rank provenance; spend capped in USD | | **Neo4j** | `llmslim[neo4j]`: `Neo4jContextStore` | Explicit tenant-scoped temporal memory: `supersede()`, `recall(as_of=...)`, `history()`, `conflicts()` | | **OpenAI** | `openai_compatible_request()`, `openai_responses_request()` | Execution-free request builders; your code sends the request | | **Anthropic Claude** | `anthropic_messages_request()` | Execution-free request builder with optional prompt-cache markers | | **Google Gemini** | `gemini_generate_request()`, `gemini_cached_content_request()` | Execution-free request builders | | **vLLM / self-hosted** | `vllm_chat_request()` | Execution-free request builder | | **OpenAI Agents SDK** | `llmslim[agents]`: `make_openai_agents_input_filter()`, `to_openai_agents_tools()` | Text-only model-input filter; the SDK keeps execution and tool ownership | | **LangChain** | `llmslim[langchain]`: `LLMSlimCompressor` | `BaseDocumentCompressor` for `ContextualCompressionRetriever` | | **LlamaIndex** | `llmslim[llamaindex]`: `LLMSlimPostprocessor` | `BaseNodePostprocessor` for query engines | | **Haystack** | `llmslim[haystack]`: `LLMSlimDocumentCompressor` | Pipeline component between retriever and prompt builder | | **gptme** | `llmslim[gptme]`: `LLMSlimContextProvider` | Context provider for gptme's compaction (entry point `llmslim`) | | **Hermes Agent** | `LLMSlimContextEngine` (no extra) | `ContextEngine` plugin; no LLM call, cache-stable prefix | | **Pydantic AI** | `llmslim[pydantic-ai]`: `llmslim_history_processor()` | History processor that keeps tool calls and returns paired |
For other frameworks there is no dedicated adapter. LLMSlim works with any framework that can pass plain message lists (`{"role": ..., "content": ...}` dicts) or document strings; you write the few lines of glue that pass LLMSlim's output to your client. --- ## 📜 License & Citation LLMSlim is open-source software licensed under the **MIT License**. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for full details. If you use LLMSlim in your research or production systems, please cite: ```bibtex @software{llmslim2026, author = {Yashvardhan Thanvi}, title = {LLMSlim: Deterministic Context Compression and Contract-Safe Tool Schemas for LLMs}, year = {2026}, publisher = {GitHub}, url = {https://github.com/Thanatos9404/llmslim} } ```
Built with precision for developers everywhere. Accepted into the Sarvam Startup Program.
--- ## Agent Context Runtime (v0.7.0) Version 0.7.0 added a per-turn context path for agent applications (0.7.0 was not published to PyPI; install 0.7.1 or later). The host supplies messages, retrieved documents, memories, tool results, and authorized tool schemas; LLMSlim returns a quality-checked model input and an explainable local trace. Model calls and tool execution stay with the host. ```python from llmslim import ContextRuntime, generic_request runtime = ContextRuntime(model="sarvam-105b", max_input_tokens=8_000) prepared = runtime.prepare_sync( user_input="When does Acme renew?", messages=[{"role": "system", "content": "Use verified dates."}], documents=[{"id": "contract", "content": "Acme renews on 9 November 2026."}], ) if prepared.feasible: request = generic_request(prepared) # the host sends this to its model print(request["messages"]) print(prepared.trace.explain()) ``` The runtime includes `ContextEnvelope`, `ContextGraph`, `ContextPolicy`, progressive planning, quality gates, bounded in-memory sessions, and execution-free adapters for generic, Sarvam, OpenAI-compatible, and text-only OpenAI Agents applications. `ContextTrace` omits prompt bodies by default. The existing `compress()` and `plan_context()` APIs continue to work. See the [architecture](docs/runtime/ARCHITECTURE.md), [security model](docs/runtime/SECURITY.md), [integrations](docs/runtime/INTEGRATIONS.md), [migration guide](docs/releases/v0.7.0-MIGRATION.md), [benchmark](docs/releases/v0.7.0-BENCHMARK.md), and [engineering report](docs/releases/v0.7.0-ENGINEERING-REPORT.md). ## Cache-Aware Context Runtime (v0.7.1) Cache planning is an opt-in layer for repeated agent turns. LLMSlim identifies stable provider-visible prefixes, keeps append-only conversation context when safe, fingerprints cache-sensitive settings, and reports local cache estimates separately from provider-reported usage. A tenant-scoped `CacheManager` stores metadata and provider references, never prompt bodies or KV tensors. ```python from llmslim import CacheManager, CachePolicy, ContextRuntime runtime = ContextRuntime( model="generic-128k", cache_policy=CachePolicy(mode="auto", provider="openai", tenant_id="my-workspace"), cache_manager=CacheManager(), ) prepared = runtime.prepare_sync( session_id="conversation-1", messages=[{"role": "system", "content": "Use verified sources."}], user_input="What changed?", ) print(prepared.trace.to_dict()["cache"]) ``` Execution-free request builders cover OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini cached resources, and self-hosted vLLM. An advanced in-process Transformers adapter validates KV continuation state. OpenAI provider-stateful continuation and Gemini cached-resource creation require explicit host opt-in. Sarvam prompt caching remains unverified and is disabled by default. The Context Inspector shows prefix segmentation and cache diagnostics without calling a provider. See [caching guidance](docs/runtime/CACHING.md), [multi-turn benchmark](docs/releases/v0.7.1-BENCHMARK.md), and [engineering report](docs/releases/v0.7.1-ENGINEERING-REPORT.md). ## Open-source security tooling [Snyk](https://snyk.io/) provides developer security tooling for open-source projects. Learn more about its [Secure Developer Program](https://snyk.io/open-source/).

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  web:
    name: Website lint and production build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: web
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: web/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run build

  server-image:
    name: Server image builds and answers
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Build the image
        run: docker build -t llmslim-server .
      - name: Refuse to start on a public interface without an API key
        run: |
          if docker run --rm llmslim-server; then echo "the server started without an API key"; exit 1; fi
      - name: Store and recall over HTTP with a key
        run: |
          KEY=$(python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))')
          docker run -d --name llmslim -p 8080:8080 -e LLMSLIM_API_KEYS="$KEY" llmslim-server
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz && break; sleep 1; done
          test "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/info)" = 401
          curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json'             -d '{"user_id": "ci", "messages": "I moved to Pune last month."}' http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/memories
          curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json'             -d '{"user_id": "ci", "query": "Where did I move to?"}' http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/memories/search | grep -q Pune
      - name: Server log
        if: always()
        run: docker logs llmslim || true

  typescript-client:
    name: TypeScript client against the server
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: clients/typescript
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: clients/typescript/package-lock.json
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Install llmslim serve for the end-to-end tests
        working-directory: .
        run: pip install -e ".[server]"
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - name: Unit and end-to-end tests
        run: npm test
        env:
          LLMSLIM_E2E_PYTHON: python
      - run: npm run build
      - name: examples/typescript-client against the server, with the published npm package
        working-directory: examples/typescript-client
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm test

  postgres-store:
    name: Memory on Postgres
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: llmslim
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: llmslim
          POSTGRES_DB: llmslim_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U llmslim"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Install llmslim with the postgres and server extras
        run: pip install -e ".[postgres,server]" pytest httpx2
      - name: Memory tests against Postgres
        env:
          LLMSLIM_TEST_POSTGRES_URL: postgresql://llmslim:llmslim@127.0.0.1:5432/llmslim_test
        run: pytest tests/test_memory.py tests/test_memory_postgres.py -o addopts="" -q -rs

  test:
    name: Test (Python ${{ matrix.python-version }} on ${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest]
        python-version: ["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            python-version: "3.12"
          - os: macos-latest
            python-version: "3.12"

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache: "pip"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip build setuptools wheel
          pip install ruff==0.15.21 mypy pytest pytest-cov twine types-PyYAML
          pip install -e ".[all,dev]"

      - name: Run Ruff Linter
        run: ruff check .

      - name: Run Ruff Code Formatter Check
        run: ruff format --check .

      - name: Run MyPy Type Checker
        if: matrix.python-version == '3.12' && matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        run: mypy llmslim

      - name: Run Pytest Suite with Coverage (Minimum 90%)
        run: pytest --cov=llmslim --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=90

      - name: Run Benchmark Smoke Test
        run: python -m benchmarks.benchmark_regression

      - name: Run Phase 2 Offline Benchmark Smoke Test
        run: python -m benchmarks.run --mode fast --no-archive

      - name: Build Package Artifacts (Wheel & Sdist)
        run: python -m build

      - name: Validate Package Artifacts
        run: twine check dist/*

      - name: Verify Clean Package Installation
        run: |
          pip install dist/*.whl
          python -c "import llmslim; print(f'llmslim version: {llmslim.__version__}')"

      - name: Upload Coverage to Codecov (Python 3.12 only)
        if: matrix.python-version == '3.12' && matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          file: ./coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

# LLMSlim memory server: memory and context over HTTP, one SQLite file, no model calls.
#   docker build -t llmslim .
#   docker run -p 8080:8080 -e LLMSLIM_API_KEYS="$(python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))')" \
#     -v llmslim-data:/data llmslim
# The server refuses to start on 0.0.0.0 without an API key.
FROM python:3.12-slim

ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR=/opt/tiktoken \
    LLMSLIM_MEMORY_DB=/data/memory.db \
    LLMSLIM_HOST=0.0.0.0 \
    LLMSLIM_PORT=8080

WORKDIR /src
COPY pyproject.toml README.md LICENSE ./
COPY llmslim ./llmslim
RUN pip install ".[server]" \
    && python -c "import tiktoken; tiktoken.get_encoding('cl100k_base')" \
    && useradd --create-home --uid 10001 llmslim \
    && mkdir -p /data \
    && chown llmslim /data

USER llmslim
WORKDIR /home/llmslim
VOLUME ["/data"]
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=10s \
    CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz', timeout=4)"
CMD ["llmslim", "serve"]

sampled_files.README.md:
# LLMSlim **Long-term memory and context selection for AI agents and coding tools, with no LLM call.** LLMSlim stores what users and agents say word for word, then returns the parts that answer a question within a token budget you set. It runs as an MCP server, a Python library or a small HTTP server. [![PyPI Version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/llmslim.svg?style=flat-square&logo=pypi&logoColor=white&color=38bdf8)](https://pypi.org/project/llmslim/) [![PyPI Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/personalized-badge/llmslim?period=total&units=INTERNATIONAL_SYSTEM&left_color=BLACK&right_color=ORANGE&left_text=downloads)](https://pepy.tech/projects/llmslim) [![MCP Registry: io.github.Thanatos9404/llmslim](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP_Registry-io.github.Thanatos9404%2Fllmslim-0098FF?style=flat-square)](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=io.github.Thanatos9404/llmslim) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-94a3b8?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![llmslim MCP server: quality and maintenance score on Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Thanatos9404/llmslim/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Thanatos9404/llmslim) [**Examples**](examples/) • [**Documentation**](https://www.llmslim.app/docs) • [**Live Studio Playground**](https://www.llmslim.app) • [**Sarvam Integration**](https://www.llmslim.app/integrations/sarvam) • [**Benchmarks**](#-benchmarks--radical-transparency) • [**Changelog**](CHANGELOG.md) A real Python session with llmslim 0.11.1 from PyPI, typed by a script and recorded with asciinema (script, recording).
## Use it in 30 seconds Each MCP setup below starts the same server, `llmslim mcp`, with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (Python 3.10 or newer). Memory goes to a local SQLite file, `~/.llmslim/memory.db`. **One click:** [![Install in VS
