      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
        python-version: ['3.11', '3.12']
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: daemon

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install -e ".[full,dev]" || pip install -e ".[dev]"

      - name: Ruff lint
        run: ruff check . --output-format=github --no-cache

      - name: Ruff format check
        run: ruff format --check . --no-cache

      - name: Run tests
        run: pip install pytest-timeout && pytest tests/ -v --tb=short --timeout=300

  # ── Frontend Linting ──
  frontend:
    name: Svelte (Prettier + Build)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: tauri-app/ui

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: tauri-app/ui/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          success=false
          for i in {1..3}; do
            if npm ci || npm install; then
              success=true
              break
            fi
            echo "Attempt $i failed, retrying in 5s..."
            sleep 5
          done
          if [ "$success" = false ]; then
            echo "Installation failed after 3 attempts"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Prettier format check
        run: npx prettier --check "src/**/*.{svelte,ts,js,css}" "vite.config.ts"

      - name: Svelte check (type checking)
        run: npx svelte-check --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json

      - name: Dependency audit
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high

      - name: Static frontend checks
        run: npm run test:static

      - name: Frontend unit tests
        run: npm run test:unit -- --run

      - name: Build check
        run: npx vite build

  approval-regression:
    name: Same-WebSocket Approval Regression
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: "pip"
          cache-dependency-path: daemon/pyproject.toml

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: tauri-app/ui/package-lock.json

      - name: Install controlled smoke dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install -e "./daemon[browser]"
          npm ci --prefix tauri-app/ui
          npm exec --prefix tauri-app/ui -- playwright install --with-deps chromium
          python -m playwright install chromium

      - name: Run deterministic approval-to-navigation regression
        working-directory: tauri-app/ui
        run: npm run test:e2e:approval -- --reporter=github
        env:
          CI: "true"

      - name: Upload approval evidence on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: approval-regression-evidence
          path: tauri-app/ui/test-results/
          retention-days: 7

  # ── Visual Regression Tests ──
  visual-regression:
    name: Visual Regression (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: tauri-app/ui
        shell: bash

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: tauri-app/ui/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          success=false
          for i in {1..3}; do
            if npm ci || npm install; then
              success=true
              break
            fi
            echo "Attempt $i failed, retrying in 5s..."
            sleep 5
          done
          if [ "$success" = false ]; then
            echo "Installation failed after 3 attempts"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Check if baselines exist for this OS
        id: check_baselines
        run: |
          # Playwright appends the OS name to snapshots (e.g. -linux.png, -win32.png, -darwin.png)
          OS_SUFFIX="linux"
          if [[ "${{ matrix.os }}" == "windows-latest" ]]; then OS_SUFFIX="win32"; fi
          if [[ "${{ matrix.os }}" == "macos-latest" ]]; then OS_SUFFIX="darwin"; fi
          echo "os_suffix=$OS_SUFFIX" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          
          SNAPSHOT_DIR="tests/visual/__snapshots__"
          if [ -n "$(find $SNAPSHOT_DIR -name "*${OS_SUFFIX}.png" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]; then
            echo "exists=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "exists=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Generate missing baseline snapshots
        if: steps.check_baselines.outputs.exists == 'false'
        run: npx playwright test --update-snapshots --reporter=github
        env:
          CI: "true"

      - name: Upload generated baselines for review
        if: steps.check_baselines.outputs.exists == 'false'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: visual-baselines-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: tauri-app/ui/tests/visual/__snapshots__/**/*-chromium-${{ steps.check_baselines.outputs.os_suffix }}.png
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Run visual regression tests (comparison)
        run: npx playwright test --reporter=github
        env:
          CI: "true"

      - name: Upload diff artifacts on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: visual-regression-diffs-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: tauri-app/ui/test-results/
          retention-days: 7

  # ── Rust Linting ──
  rust:
    name: Rust (Clippy + Fmt)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            libgtk-3-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev

      - name: Install Rust stable
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt

      - name: Rust cache
        uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: "tauri-app/src-tauri -> target"

      # Build frontend first (Tauri needs it)
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: tauri-app/ui/package-lock.json

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: tauri-app/ui
        run: |
          success=false
          for i in {1..3}; do
            if npm ci || npm install; then
              success=true
              break
            fi
            echo "Attempt $i failed, retrying in 5s..."
            sleep 5
          done
          if [ "$success" = false ]; then
            echo "Installation failed after 3 attempts"
            exit 1
          fi
          npx vite build

      - name: Cargo fmt check
        working-directory: tauri-app/src-tauri
        run: cargo fmt -- --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        working-directory: tauri-app/src-tauri
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo tests
        working-directory: tauri-app/src-tauri
        run: cargo test --all-targets

# Heliox OS — AI System Control Agent

Control your computer with natural language, voice, and opt-in gestures.
Heliox plans supported work, applies permission gates, executes it locally, and verifies the result.

Website • Download • Evidence • Compare • Sponsor

## What Heliox is Heliox OS is an MIT-licensed, local-first desktop agent for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It translates typed or spoken requests into validated plans, routes actions to specialist providers, asks before risky or irreversible work, and reports completion only through the guarded execution path. Heliox is an application that runs on top of an existing operating system; it is not an operating-system kernel. Local-first also does not mean every configuration is offline: cloud models and third-party integrations receive the context required for tasks that use them. **Name disambiguation:** Heliox OS is this desktop-agent project at `helioxos.dev` and `VyomKulshrestha/Heliox-OS`. It is unrelated to heliox helium-oxygen medical gas and to other products named Heliox, including Heliox IDE. ```text User intent → Planner → Permission and risk gates → Specialist → Executor → Verifier ↘ durable task state, memory, audit, cancellation and recovery ↗ ``` Published release: **v0.14.0** · Python **3.11+** · Windows is the primary hardware-development platform. v0.14.0 adds a consented assistance co-adaptation study, accessibility-grounded desktop control with human takeover, restart-surviving and scheduled autonomous jobs, tools from your own MCP servers, voice-first control while a task runs, and fail-closed settings, gateway profiles and approvals. Provider subscriptions, integrations, peers, hardware inputs, and host actions remain subject to their documented availability and safety boundaries. ## Why Heliox - **Acts instead of only answering:** supported browser, desktop, file, process, package, Git, integration, screen, and workflow operations enter a real execution path. - **Verifies instead of assuming:** results pass through executor contracts, and selected actions also have independent post-condition checks. - **Keeps authority explicit:** five permission tiers, irreversibility flags, per-action approvals, source-scoped gateway policy, cancellation, and fail-closed snapshot requirements bound risky work. - **Coordinates multiple inputs:** text, continuous voice, gesture, gaze, screen context, and experimental neural intent share one priority-controlled interaction path. - **Runs locally by default:** the daemon, action execution, preferences, audit stores, and supported local models remain on the user's computer. - **Exposes evidence:** capability coverage, limitations, benchmark data, CI, release feeds, and machine-readable metadata are public. ## Evidence snapshot | Surface | Current evidence | Important See the [transparent cost page](https://www.helioxos.dev/cost.html) for software, provider, model-download, and hardware costs. ## Core capabilities | Capability | Implemented behavior | | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Guarded task execution | Typed plans, source-scoped policy, approvals, cancellation, execution claims, and visible terminal results | | Adaptive app tasks | Bounded observe → act → verify loops with fresh screen evidence, target-window reacquisition, replanning, and no-progress termination | | Continuous voice | Faster-Whisper/OpenAI Whisper recognition, adaptive-noise VAD with pre-roll, wake-word and follow-up listening, coordinated TTS, barge-in, self-speech suppression, and a non-executing microphone test | | Interactive companion | Can warn, revise, stop, accept spoken or typed corrections, answer explicit questions without cancelling a running task, and offer grounded next steps after verified results | | Local chat sessions | Separate transcripts and task context with bounded cross-session preference and evidence memory | | Gesture and gaze | 30+ gesture mappings, MediaPipe Tasks 3D landmarks, coarse gaze fusion, calibration, temporal rejection, and opt-in cursor control | | Background workflows | Durable jobs with pause, resume, cancellation, restart recovery, and guarded autonomous execution | | Hybrid risk model | Deterministic policy plus structured transitions, learned risk, executor-callback history, verified outcome adaptation, and optional shadow UI-JEPA; learned output can only add caution | | Assistance co-adaptation | Opt-in, consented selection study inside Heliox's window: a world model of the person, the interface and Heliox predicts which help (larger targets, a confirm step, a clarifying question, another input) suits this person today, within rules the person sets; it changes presentation only and never approves or runs anything | | Per-task undo | Before a file write, move, copy or delete, a clipboard change, an environment variable, or a volume or brightness change, Heliox keeps what it needs to reverse it. Each finished task's message in chat has **Undo** and **Verify receipt**. After the task, **Review undo** shows what will be put back, what you changed since (left alone) and what can never be undone (messages, web actions, commands); the approval dialog marks each action "Can undo" or "Can't undo" | | Bounded learning | Provenance-aware temporal memory, repeated-evidence promotion, replay, drift detection, and reset controls | | Plugin ecosystem | Reviewed GitHub marketplace, signed local plugins, per-file hashes, capability manifests, and constrained native/WASM brokers | | Neural research | BrainFlow synthetic, recorded EEG playback, public EEGBCI benchmarking, calibrated SSVEP selection, replay-safe Tier 0/1 goals, and explicit staged autonomous task launch | | MCP interfaces | Public read-only documentation MCP plus a local, separately authenticated stdio bridge whose tasks use visible Heliox approvals | | Air Handoff | Opt-in same-LAN phone pairing and one-target encrypted transfer of a held screenshot, text value, or immutable file snapshot. Optionally, a paired phone can send a request that waits for **Run** on the computer; status checks can start at once and answer back to the phone. The phone never approves anything | | Signed task receipts | After each task that ran actions, an Ed25519-signed, hash-chained receipt of what ran, what you approved and what happened; contents appear only as hashes, and `python -m pilot.workflows.task_receipts verify` checks one anywhere | | Today view and brief | A Today tab shows what Heliox ran, where your time went and what can still be undone, with Undo on each task; an opt-in daily brief arrives at the time you choose, as a notification and in chat, optionally read aloud. "Undo the last two tasks" opens each task's undo preview in turn | | Command palette | Ctrl+K (or "what can I say?") lists every built-in command with working examples and your recent requests; choosing one fills the command box so you can check it before it runs | | Notes, nudges, settings | "Note that the plumber comes Tuesday" / "read my notes"; "tell me if I spend more than an hour on YouTube today" (once a day, from the activity timeline, nothing blocked); "turn on the activity timeline" or "send me a daily brief at 7 pm" by voice (security settings never change by voice) | | Setups and history | "Save this as my coding setup" remembers which apps are open and "open my coding setup" brings them back (with normal approvals); "when did I ask you to email the invoice?" searches your task history; "set a timer for 10 minutes" | | Focus and reports | "Start a pomodoro", quiet hours ("focus every weekday from 9 to 12") and "say that again"; "Focus for 45 minutes" holds reminders and the brief and keeps Heliox quiet (approvals still come through), then gives one summary of where the time went; the Today tab adds **This week** and **Export report** (Markdown with every task and its receipt id) | | Reminders and recall | "Remind me in 20 minutes to stretch" or "tomorrow at 9 to send the report" (kept across restarts, spoken when due); "where did you put my report?" from what Heliox moved or saved; **Show what changed** in the undo preview gives a line-by-line diff of each file Heliox wrote | | Routines and shortcuts | "Do that every day at 9" turns the last task into a routine that may use only the actions that task used (you confirm on screen); "when I say start work, open VS Code and Slack" creates a voice shortcut; "do that again" repeats the last task with fresh approvals | | Activity timeline | Opt-in local record of which app and window title were in front, so "what was I working on yesterday afternoon?" gets an answer by voice or chat (and "what did you do today?" is answered from receipts); never pixels or screen text, password managers and private windows skipped | | Secure integrations | Settings-managed CalDAV, IMAP/SMTP, and allowlisted SSH connections with secrets kept in the operating-system credential store | While a task runs, choose **Ask without stopping** to ask a question, **Correct task** to interrupt the current step and replan, or **Queue next task** to submit another task for execution afterward. Spoken “quick question …”, status questions, and “next task …” use the corresponding paths. Queued interactive tasks are serialized through the normal approval and verification gates; they are not parallel desktop controllers. The passive screen monitor tracks the active window and visual changes; it does not continuously understand every pixel. “Read my screen” invokes local OCR on demand. Screen context never grants an action or bypasses approval. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Input[Text · voice · gesture · gaze] --> Gateway[Interaction gateway] Gateway --> Planner[Planner + context] Planner --> Safety[Policy · risk · approval] Safety --> Mesh[21-specialist mesh] Mesh --> Executor[Shared executor] Executor --> Verifier[Outcome verifier] Verifier --> Result[Visible result] Verifier --> Memory[Ledger · memory · replay] Memory --> Planner Neurod[Synthetic / recorded / local neural sidecar] --> NeuralSelect[Bounded neural selection] NeuralSelect --> Gateway MCPHost[Local MCP host] --> MCPBridge[Least-privilege stdio bridge] MCPBridge --> Safety Safety --> Handoff[Explicit one-target Air Handoff] ``` The desktop is a Tauri/Svelte application. A local Python daemon owns planning, permissions, specialist routing, execution, verification, durable state, memory, and model adapters. Browser, OS, integration, plugin, and research paths enter the same safety and audit backbone. - [Architecture and process boundaries](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - [IPC message formats](IPC_MESSAGE_FORMATS.md) - [Agent development guide](AGENT_DEVELOPMENT_GUIDE.md) ## Security and privacy > [!WARNING] > Heliox can execute code, modify files, control applications, and invoke external services. Do not run it as root or Administrator for ordinary work. Review approval dialogs, keep backups, and treat model output as untrusted until execution evidence confirms the requested result. Core guarantees: - Structured schema validation before execution. - Five permission tiers plus a separate irreversibility flag for effects that snapshots cannot undo. - Per-action approval for system-modifying, destructive, root-critical, and irreversible work. An approval that is never answered, or whose reply never reaches the window, expires instead of running; a plan resumed after a restart runs only the actions that were ticked. - A gesture can approve only a dialog that has been visible for a second, and only the ticked actions. - Source-scoped gateway floors that a task override may narrow but cannot widen; an action family a profile does not list is read-only. - Snapshot requirements that fail closed when a required backend is unavailable. - Per-task undo computed in code, never by a model: it restores only what Heliox recorded, skips anything changed since, needs a click on the preview you saw, and never runs while a task is running. - HMAC-chained audit records for elevated permission and gateway decisions. - Real cancellation of in-flight commands and durable reconciliation after reconnect or restart. - Learned risk, cognitive estimates, adaptation, and neural input cannot grant permission or remove deterministic warnings. - OS credential stores for API keys; credentials are never written to `.env` or included in plans. - Air Handoff is off by default; a paired phone can receive only content explicitly held and dropped to it, never daemon RPC or desktop-control authority. Phone requests are a separate opt-in: they wait for Run on the computer, and only a fixed list of status checks may start without you. - Every task that ran actions leaves a signed, hash-chained receipt; the activity timeline is off by default and never stores pixels or screen text. - Gesture cursor control is off by default and exits on an open palm, stop control, or disabled setting. - Assistance co-adaptation is off by default and stores nothing without a per-purpose consent record. Its data is encrypted with a per-participant key in the OS keyring, and revoking, expiry or erasing deletes the data and the key. It never commits an ambiguous selection by guessing. | Tier | Level | Default behavior | Examples | | ---- | ------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | 0 | Read only | Auto-execute | `file_read`, `system_info`, `clipboard_read` | | 1 | User write | Auto-execute | `file_write`, `clipboard_write`, `env_set` | | 2 | System modify | Confirm | `package_install`, `service_restart`, `wifi_connect` | | 3 | Destructive | Confirm | `file_delete`, `process_kill`, `power_shutdown` | | 4 | Root critical | Confirm | privileged and disk operations | Some lower-tier effects—such as sending email, invoking a remote SSH command, or pushing a commit—are still irreversible and therefore require confirmation. Read [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the threat model, rollback boundaries, supervision controls, and responsible disclosure process. Read the [privacy policy](https://www.helioxos.dev/privacy.html) before enabling cloud models or integrations. ## Installation ### Download the desktop application 1. Open the [latest GitHub release](https://github.com/VyomKulshrestha/Heliox-OS/releases). 2. Download the package for your system: - Windows: `Heliox-OS__x64-setup.exe` or `.msi` - macOS Apple Silicon: `Heliox-OS__aarch64.dmg` - macOS Intel: `Heliox-OS__x64.dmg` - Linux: `.AppImage`, `.deb`, or `.rpm` 3. Install and open Heliox OS. 4. Select a local model, add a provider key, or connect an eligible Codex/Claude Code subscription in Settings. The desktop application requires Python 3.11 or newer and starts the local daemon automatically. First launch may take longer while Heliox creates its environment and downloads optional components. The UI continues reconnecting during initialization. Windows installers are not yet production-signed. The SignPath test workflow is validated, but Windows may continue to show reputation warnings until the production certificate is issued and connected to the release workflow. ### Build from source ```bash git clone https://github.com/VyomKulshrestha/Heliox-OS.git cd Heliox-OS/daemon python -m pip install -e ".[all,dev]" python -m pilot.server ``` In a separate terminal: ```bash cd Heliox-OS/tauri-app/ui npm ci npm run dev ``` To run the native desktop shell: ```bash cd Heliox-OS/tauri-app npm install npm run tauri dev ``` Windows contributors can use `setup.ps1`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for platform prerequisites and test commands. ### Connect a local MCP host Start the Heliox desktop application, then configure an MCP host to launch the installed `heliox-mcp` command: ```json { "mcpServers": { "heliox-local": { "command": "heliox-mcp" } } } ``` The local server exposes status, capabilities, task preview, submission, polling, cancellation, and optional local research-only typed-decision scoring with [Gnomon](docs/GNOMON_TRAINING.md) for single or batched questions. Every submitted action requires visible approval in Heliox; neither the MCP client nor the research scorer can approve its own work. See [MCP interfaces](docs/MCP.md) for the tool list and security boundary. ### Give Heliox tools from other MCP servers Heliox is also an MCP client. List servers in `mcp_servers.json` inside Heliox's config folder, in the same format, and the planner can call their tools (GitHub, Slack, Notion, databases and so on) as ordinary actions: ```json { "mcpServers": { "github": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"], "env": { "GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN": "..." } } } } ``` Tools the server marks read-only run straight away; every other tool asks for approval with its arguments shown. Call `mcp_client_refresh` (or restart the daemon) after editing the file. ## Try these tasks ```text Show me my system information. Open an installed application and verify its window appears. Go to Wikipedia's artificial-intelligence page and summarize the introduction. Create a Python project with tests and run them. Monitor CPU usage and alert me above 80%. List every Python file on my Desktop. Take a screenshot and read the visible text. Set my volume to 50%. ``` Risky and irreversible tasks may pause for approval. A completed plan is not by itself proof that the requested environmental outcome occurred. ## Configuration User configuration is stored at `~/.config/heliox-os/config.toml`. Most settings are also available in the desktop Settings panel. ```toml [model] provider = "ollama" # "ollama", "cloud", or "subscription" ollama_model = "llama3.1:8b" cloud_provider = "gemini" # "gemini", "openai", "openrouter", "claude", or "meta" cloud_model = "" # OpenRouter defaults to "openrouter/auto"; try "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro" subscription_provider = "codex" # "codex" or "claude" subscription_model = "" # blank uses the official CLI default subscription_timeout_seconds = 120 subscription_max_prompt_chars = 48000 [security] root_enabled = false snapshot_on_destructive = true [vision] mediapipe_backend = "tasks" gaze_tracking_enabled = false [gesture_cursor] enabled = false [voice] transcription_engine = "auto" whisper_model = "small" language = "auto" tts_engine = "kokoro_tts" [undo] enabled = true # keep what is needed to undo file and clipboard changes retention_days = 7 max_task_mb = 512 # larger changes still run, but are listed as not undoable max_total_mb = 2048 [receipts] enabled = true retention_days = 90 [timeline] enabled = false # app and window-title history for "what was I working on?" retention_days = 7 [brief] enabled = false # one summary of the day at `time` time = "18:00" speak = false [co_adaptation] enabled = false # the selection study; also needs a consent record per participant adaptive_enabled = false # learned choices from the second session; also needs the adaptive_assistance purpose learn_across_sessions = false ambiguity_threshold = 0.25 # may only be made stricter; never learned ``` OpenRouter uses its OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Settings and first-run setup offer automatic routing, DeepSeek V4 Pro, the latest DeepSeek V4 Flash alias, and other current aliases; an exact OpenRouter catalog model ID can also be entered manually. Provider keys remain in the operating-system credential store. ### Use an existing Codex or Claude subscription Install and sign in through the provider's official CLI (`codex login` or `claude auth login`), then choose **Existing AI subscription** in first-run setup or Settings. Heliox does not copy browser sessions, read OAuth files, or store these credentials. The CLI runs as a text-only model helper in a sterile temporary directory; Codex is read-only and ephemeral, while Claude has tools, browser integration, slash commands, and session persistence disabled. Heliox still owns schema validation, policy, approval, execution, and verification. See the official [Codex with ChatGPT plan guide](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11369540-using-codex-with-your-chatgpt-plan) and [Claude Code authentication guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication) for provider-owned installation and login requirements. The provider CLI adds its own instruction overhead. Settings separates the Heliox prompt estimate from provider-reported input, cached input, uncached input, and output. Exact repeated requests use Heliox's response cache and do not consume provider quota. The prompt-context cap prevents unbounded history; simple deterministic commands continue to use local fast paths with zero model calls. Subscription allowance and model availability remain governed by the user's provider plan, not by Heliox. Run the optional planning-only benchmark from `daemon/` to measure latency, plan quality, and reported usage without executing any proposed action: ```bash python benchmarks/subscription_planning_suite.py --provider codex ``` Kokoro, Pocket TTS, gaze, gesture tracking, and the learned-risk model are CPU-capable; CUDA is not required. Kokoro and Pocket synthesis runs in a short-lived worker that remains available for a 10-second speech burst, then exits so PyTorch/CUDA libraries do not stay mapped in the control daemon. Optional models still consume storage, memory, CPU time, and download bandwidth while active. ## Platform and research boundaries | Surface | Current status | | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Windows 10/11 | Primary development and hardware-validation platform | | Ubuntu/Debian | Python/UI CI plus desktop packages; integrations and permissions vary | | macOS | Python/UI CI plus desktop packages; permissions and hardware require local validation | | Camera gesture and gaze | Automated geometry, calibration, fusion, and false-positive tests; physical accuracy is not established across users and environments | | Voice and TTS | Routing, fallback, interruption, cancellation, synthetic ASR, and non-executing microphone-test coverage; human microphone accuracy and audible quality still require human checks | | Neural intent | Synthetic BrainFlow and recorded EEG paths are tested. A user may stage up to eight text-authored goals and use calibrated focus/select to launch one through normal autonomous decomposition, specialist routing, permissions, approvals, and verification. No live headset accuracy, unrestricted thought reading, medical use, or physical authority is established. | | Cognitive HUD | Behavioural estimates from local interaction signals, not physiological or medical measurements | | Assistance co-adaptation | Model, policy, consent store and in-app study are built and tested; every published result comes from simulated users. No claim about people until the pre-registered human study reports. EEG is not part of it. | | Air Handoff | Automated pairing, cryptography, replay, expiry, file-snapshot, and browser-receiver tests pass. A real phone, LAN/firewall, QR scan, and mobile download still require a human hardware/network check. | ## Troubleshooting | Problem | First check | | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Daemon remains offline | Confirm Python 3.11+, inspect `~/.local/state/heliox-os/pilot.log`, and ensure port 8785 is free | | Provider key is rejected | Re-enter it through Settings and confirm the OS credential store is available; Heliox does not use `.env` keys | | Voice or camera is unavailable | Grant OS/WebView permission, select the correct device, and close other applications using that hardware | | Installed application is not found | Use its installed display name; missing or ambiguous application matches fail visibly | | Optional Windows model reports missing DLLs | Install the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable and reinstall the relevant daemon extra in 64-bit Python | Open a [bug report](https://github.com/VyomKulshrestha/Heliox-OS/issues/new/choose) with the operating system, Heliox version, logs, expected result, and observed result. Hardware-dependent reports should also include the device and environment. ## Documentation - [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - [MCP interfaces and local-host setup](docs/MCP.md) - [Security policy and threat model](SECURITY.md) - [Windows signing](docs/WINDOWS_SIGNING.md) - [Gesture and gaze control](GESTURES.md) - [Plugin marketplace](docs/PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE.md) - [Neural intent research controls](docs/NEURAL_INTENT.md) - [Intelligence evaluation and research map](docs/INTELLIGENCE_EVALUATION.md) - [Assistance co-adaptation: model, consent and evidence](docs/COADAPTATION.md) - [Opt-in recorded workflows and local visual samples](docs/RECORDED_WORKFLOWS.md) - [Gnomon typed-decision model: training, gates and results](docs/GNOMON_TRAINING.md) - [Public decision-corpus adaptation log](docs/PUBLIC_CORPUS_ADAPTATION.md) - [Forensics runbook](docs/FORENSICS_RUNBOOK.md) - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Website agent index](https://www.helioxos.dev/llms.txt) and [repository agent index](llms.txt) - [CodeMeta](codemeta.json), [citation metadata](CITATION.cff), and [machine-readable releases](releases.json) ### Agent and search discovery Heliox publishes public, read-only discovery surfaces so search engines and assistants can inspect current capabilities and limitations instead of inferring them from marketing copy: - [Agent index](https://www.helioxos.dev/llms.txt) and [machine-readable capabilities](https://www.helioxos.dev/capabilities.json) - [Public OpenAPI document](https://www.helioxos.dev/openapi.json) and [API catalog](https://www.helioxos.dev/.well-known/api-catalog) - [Read-only documentation MCP manifest](https://www.helioxos.dev/.well-known/mcp.json) - [Agent skills index](https://www.helioxos.dev/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json) - [Human evidence center](https://www.helioxos.dev/proof.html), [Markdown evidence](https://www.helioxos.dev/proof.md), and [release feed](https://www.helioxos.dev/releases.json) These surfaces improve technical discoverability; they do not guarantee search ranking, citations, sponsorship, or funding. External visibility is measured separately through a recurring prompt and index audit. The public documentation MCP is intentionally unable to control a computer. Local control uses the separately authenticated stdio bridge documented in [MCP interfaces](docs/MCP.md), and its work remains approval-gated in the desktop application. ## Support Heliox Heliox is free and open source. Sponsorship funds the physical validation that software-only CI cannot provide: microphones, cameras, accessibility devices, EEG acquisition hardware, clean-machine release testing, and cross-platform systems. - [Sponsor through GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/VyomKulshrestha) - [Read the funding goals and reporting policy](docs/SPONSORING.md) - Lend test hardware, contribute code, or publish reproducible hardware results - Connect the project with accessibility, human-computer interaction, or neurotechnology laboratories Sponsorship never purchases security exceptions, private user data, approval bypasses, or control over technical results. ## Contributing 1. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). 2. Choose a [good first issue](https://github.com/VyomKulshrestha/Heliox-OS/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good%20first%20issue%22). 3. Review the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). 4. Join [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/VyomKulshrestha/Heliox-OS/discussions). ## License Heliox OS is available under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

Getting Started

**Enable completion alerts:** run `/config` inside Claude Code and choose a notification channel such as **Terminal bell**.

Quick Start

> [!TIP] > **Run claude in a project directory to start the interface.** > > **Go to [Help & Troubleshooting](#help--troubleshooting) to fix issues...** **Native installer (recommended; no Node.js required)** macOS, Linux, or WSL: ```bash curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ``` Windows PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` Windows CMD: ```bat curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.cmd -o install.cmd && install.cmd && del install.cmd ``` Supported package managers (manual updates by default): ```bash brew install --cask claude-code winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode ``` npm distribution (supported; Node.js 22+ is required to install): ```bash npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code ``` Verify the installation, then start Claude Code: ```bash claude --version claude doctor claude ``` Native installs update themselves. Homebrew, WinGet, and the signed `apt`, `dnf`, and `apk` repositories follow their package manager's update flow. See the [official setup guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) for channels, version pinning, Linux repository setup, and signature verification. For an npm install, upgrade with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest`; do not use `sudo npm install -g`. --- > [!Tip] > **Open Project Via Terminal Into VS Code / Cursor** > > ### $ - cd /path/to/project > > ### $ - code . > > **Make sure you have the (Claude Code extension) installed in your VS Code / Cursor** ---

System Requirements

> - OS: macOS 13+, Windows 10 1809+/Windows Server 2019+, Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+, or Alpine Linux 3.19+. Native Windows, WSL 1, and WSL 2 are supported. > - Hardware: 4 GB+ RAM and an x64 or ARM64 processor > - Software: Git is optional on native Windows; without Git for Windows, Claude uses the PowerShell tool instead of Bash. Node.js 22+ is required only to install through npm; the installed CLI is a native binary. > - Internet: Connection for API calls ---

Initial Setup

Claude Code requires a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, or Console account; the free Claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code. The normal first-party flow is browser sign-in: ```bash claude auth login # Claude subscription claude auth login --console # Anthropic Console/API billing claude auth status # Verify the active login ``` For API automation or a provider/gateway deployment, inject credentials from an OS key store or secret manager instead of committing them: ```bash export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$SECRET_FROM_YOUR_STORE" # bash/zsh: current process only ``` ```powershell $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = $secretFromYourStore # PowerShell: current process only ``` > [!Important] > A persistent `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or credential helper selects API/provider authentication even if you are logged in. Subscription-only features such as Remote Control, cloud sessions, claude.ai MCP connectors, and notification preferences then remain unavailable. Do not commit credentials; use your platform's secret storage. ---

Configuration & Environment

Environment Variables

> **Environment values can also be stored as strings under the `env` key in a `settings.json` file. The [official environment-variable reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) is the exhaustive source.** > [!Important] > **On PowerShell, use `$env:NAME = "value"` for the current process. Persist secrets through an OS key store or secret manager, not a checked-in settings file.** ```bash # Authentication and routing: set only when API/provider billing is intentional export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$SECRET_FROM_YOUR_STORE" export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$TOKEN_FROM_YOUR_STORE" export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://gateway.example.com" export ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS="X-Trace-Id: 12345" # Model selection and provider alias overrides export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="sonnet" export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL="" export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="" export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="" export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="" # Third-party provider selection (enable only one deployment path) # export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 # export ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX=eu # Prefer eu/us/apac/jp/au/global cross-region inference on Bedrock # export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1 # export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1 # Timeouts and output budgets, in milliseconds/tokens export API_TIMEOUT_MS=1200000 export BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 export BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 export MCP_TIMEOUT=30000 export MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT=60000 export MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS=25000 export MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 # 0 disables fixed thinking where supported; positive values set a budget # Session, context, agents, and accessibility # export CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1 # export CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE=1 export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1 # Clamp native-1M models to 200K via autocompaction; warns if the clamp is not enforced export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_UNKNOWN_MODEL_WINDOW_ENFORCEMENT=1 # Opt out of enforcing the assumed context window for unknown model IDs export CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS=20 export CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=3 export CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT=1 export CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1 # Feature and administration controls export CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 export CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 export CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1 export CLAUDE_CODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER_AUTO_UPDATE=1 export ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false # Network routing export HTTP_PROXY="http://proxy.example.com:8080" export HTTPS_PROXY="http://proxy.example.com:8080" export NO_PROXY="localhost,127.0.0.1" # Privacy/network reduction: these are presence-based; unset them to turn them off export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 export DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 export DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1 ``` The block is a catalog, not a recommended profile—do not enable mutually exclusive provider variables together. Boolean variables usually accept `1`/`true` and `0`/`false`, but the three presence-based variables shown at the end treat any non-empty value, including `0`, as enabled. Environment values in `settings.json` override the shell value at startup and when the file changes.

Global Config Options

Use `/config` for interactive settings, or pass one or more `key=value` pairs. Run `/config --help` for the keys supported by your installed build. ```bash /config # Open the settings UI /config theme=dark model=sonnet # Update supported keys directly ``` For version-controlled or managed configuration, edit JSON settings files directly: | Scope | File | | :---- | :--- | | User | `~/.claude/settings.json` | | Project (shared) | `.claude/settings.json` | | Project (private) | `.claude/settings.local.json` | | Managed | macOS: `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/`
Linux/WSL: `/etc/claude-code/`
Windows: `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\` | ```json { "model": "sonnet", "theme": "dark", "autoUpdatesChannel": "stable", "permissions": { "defaultMode": "default" } } ``` Settings precedence is **managed policy → CLI arguments/`--settings` → local → project → user**. Permission arrays have their own merge rules, so read the [settings reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings) before relying on ordinary last-writer-wins behavior. `~/.claude.json` stores global state, session/trust data, and local/user MCP configuration; it is not the user settings file.

Configuration Files

Claude Code combines human-authored instructions from several locations: | Memory Type | Location | Purpose | Use Case Examples | Shared With | | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | | **Enterprise policy** | macOS: `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md`
Linux: `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md`
Windows: `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md` | Organization-wide instructions managed by IT/DevOps | Company coding standards, security policies, compliance requirements | All users in organization | | **Project memory** | `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Team-shared instructions for the project | Project architecture, coding standards, common workflows | Team members via source control | | **User memory** | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Personal preferences for all projects | Code styling preferences, personal tooling shortcuts | Just you (all projects) | | **Project memory (local)** | `./CLAUDE.local.md` | Personal project-specific preferences (git-ignored) | Your sandbox URLs, preferred test data, personal overrides | Just you (current project) | | **Project rules** | `.claude/rules/**/*.md` | Modular project rules (loaded alongside CLAUDE.md) | Linting rules, API conventions, path-scoped standards | Team members via source control | > Instruction files are concatenated rather than overriding one another. User and ancestor-project files load at startup; `CLAUDE.md` files in subdirectories load lazily when Claude works there. `CLAUDE.md` is context, not an enforcement boundary. Use `@path` to import another file. Claude Code does not load `AGENTS.md` automatically; add `@AGENTS.md` to `CLAUDE.md` (or use a symlink where portable) when you want to share those instructions. #### `.claude/rules/` Directory The `.claude/rules/` directory lets you break project instructions into separate Markdown files instead of one large `CLAUDE.md`. Markdown files are discovered recursively. Add `paths` frontmatter with glob patterns when a rule should load only for matching files. This is useful for: - **Modular organization**: Separate concerns (e.g., `api-conventions.md`, `testing-rules.md`) - **Per-directory overrides**: Nested `rules/` directories can apply scoped rules - **Team collaboration**: Different team members can own different rule files via PR review #### Auto-Memory Claude can save useful working context under `~/.claude/projects//memory/`. It loads the first 200 lines or 25 KB of `MEMORY.md`; use `/memory` to inspect, edit, disable, or remove saved memories. Auto-memory is machine-local and shared across worktrees for the same repository. Auto-memory is most useful for context you would otherwise repeat across sessions: - Preferred build, test, and lint commands - Local conventions that are not obvious from code alone - Architecture decisions that influence future edits - Team preferences that should shape how Claude proposes changes Keep durable team rules in `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/rules/`. Treat auto-memory as helpful working context, not as the only source of truth. ---

Commands & Usage

Slash Command Reference

Type `/` to see what your installed build, plan, platform, plugins, MCP servers, and skills actually provide. The table below is a high-value snapshot; use the [official command reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands) for the live list. | Command | Purpose | | :------ | :------ | | `/add-dir ` | Grant this session access to another working directory | | `/advisor [model\|off]` | Configure the experimental second-model advisor, save the selection, or turn it off | | `/agents` | Explain how to create or edit subagents; the old interactive agent wizard was removed in v2.1.198 | | `/background [prompt]` | Detach the current conversation as a background session (`/bg` alias) | | `/batch ` | Decompose a large change into worktree-isolated background units (bundled skill) | | `/branch [name]` | Switch into a new branch of the current conversation while preserving the original | | `/btw [question]` | Ask an ephemeral side question without adding it to conversation history | | `/cd ` | Move the current session to another working directory | | `/clear [name]` | Start a new conversation with empty context while preserving project memory | | `/code-review [level] [--fix] [--comment] [target]` | Run a local background review, or use level `ultra` for cloud review; levels run from `low` through `max` | | `/compact [instructions]` | Summarize the conversation to free context | | `/config [key=value ...]` | Open settings or update supported keys directly (`/settings` alias) | | `/context [all]` | Visualize what is using the context window | | `/diff` | Open the interactive current/per-turn diff viewer | | `/doctor` | Diagnose setup, configuration, hooks, memory, plugins, and MCP; Getting Started

**Enable completion alerts:** run `/config` inside Claude Code and choose a notification channel such as **Terminal bell**.

Quick Start

> [!TIP] > **Run claude in a project directory to start the interface.** > > **Go to [Help & Troubleshooting](#help--troubleshooting) to fix issues...** **Native installer (recommended; no Node.js required)** macOS, Linux, or WSL: ```bash curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ``` Windows PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` Windows CMD: ```bat curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.cmd -o install.cmd && install.cmd && del install.cmd ``` Supported package managers (manual updates by default): ```bash brew install --cask claude-code winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode ``` npm distribution (supported; Node.js 22+ is required to install): ```bash npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code ``` Verify the installation, then start Claude Code: ```bash claude --version claude doctor claude ``` Native installs update themselves. Homebrew, WinGet, and the signed `apt`, `dnf`, and `apk` repositories follow their package manager's update flow. See the [official setup guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) for channels, version pinning, Linux repository setup, and signature verification. For an npm install, upgrade with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest`; do not use `sudo npm install -g`. --- > [!Tip] > **Open Project Via Terminal Into VS Code / Cursor** > > ### $ - cd /path/to/project > > ### $ - code . > > **Make sure you have the (Claude Code extension) installed in your VS Code / Cursor** ---

System Requirements

> - OS: macOS 13+, Windows 10 1809+/Windows Server 2019+, Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+, or Alpine Linux 3.19+. Native Windows, WSL 1, and WSL 2 are supported. > - Hardware: 4 GB+ RAM and an x64 or ARM64 processor > - Software: Git is optional on native Windows; without Git for Windows, Claude uses the PowerShell tool instead of Bash. Node.js 22+ is required only to install through npm; the installed CLI is a native binary. > - Internet: Connection for API calls ---

Initial Setup

Claude Code requires a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, or Console account; the free Claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code. The normal first-party flow is browser sign-in: ```bash claude auth login # Claude subscription claude auth login --console # Anthropic Console/API billing claude auth status # Verify the active login ``` For API automation or a provider/gateway deployment, inject credentials from an OS key store or secret manager instead of committing them: ```bash export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$SECRET_FROM_YOUR_STORE" # bash/zsh: current process only ``` ```powershell $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = $secretFromYourStore # PowerShell: current process only ``` > [!Important] > A persistent `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or credential helper selects API/provider authentication even if you are logged in. Subscription-only features such as Remote Control, cloud sessions, claude.ai MCP connectors, and notification preferences then remain unavailable. Do not commit credentials; use your platform's secret storage. ---

Configuration & Environment

Environment Variables

> **Environment values can also be stored as strings under the `env` key in a `settings.json` file. The [official environment-variable reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) is the exhaustive source.** > [!Important] > **On PowerShell, use `$env:NAME = "value"` for the current process. Persist secrets through an OS key store or secret manager, not a checked-in settings file.** ```bash # Authentication and routing: set only when API/provider billing is intentional export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$SECRET_FROM_YOUR_STORE" export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$TOKEN_FROM_YOUR_STORE" export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://gateway.example.com" export ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS="X-Trace-Id: 12345" # Model selection and provider alias overrides export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="sonnet" export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL="" export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="" export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="" export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="" # Third-party provider selection (enable only one deployment path) # export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 # export ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX=eu # Prefer eu/us/apac/jp/au/global cross-region inference on Bedrock # export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1 # export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1 # Timeouts and output budgets, in milliseconds/tokens export API_TIMEOUT_MS=1200000 export BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 export BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 export MCP_TIMEOUT=30000 export MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT=60000 export MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS=25000 export MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 # 0 disables fixed thinking where supported; positive values set a budget # Session, context, agents, and accessibility # export CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1 # export CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE=1 export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1 # Clamp native-1M models to 200K via autocompaction; warns if the clamp is not enforced export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_UNKNOWN_MODEL_WINDOW_ENFORCEMENT=1 # Opt out of enforcing the assumed context window for unknown model IDs export CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS=20 export CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=3 export CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT=1 export CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1 # Feature and administration controls export CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 export CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 export CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1 export CLAUDE_CODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER_AUTO_UPDATE=1 export ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false # Network routing export HTTP_PROXY="http://proxy.example.com:8080" export HTTPS_PROXY="http://proxy.example.com:8080" export NO_PROXY="localhost,127.0.0.1" # Privacy/network reduction: these are presence-based; unset them to turn them off export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 export DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 export DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1 ``` The block is a catalog, not a recommended profile—do not enable mutually exclusive provider variables together. Boolean variables usually accept `1`/`true` and `0`/`false`, but the three presence-based variables shown at the end treat any non-empty value, including `0`, as enabled. Environment values in `settings.json` override the shell value at startup and when the file changes.

Global Config Options

Use `/config` for interactive settings, or pass one or more `key=value` pairs. Run `/config --help` for the keys supported by your installed build. ```bash /config # Open the settings UI /config theme=dark model=sonnet # Update supported keys directly ``` For version-controlled or managed configuration, edit JSON settings files directly: | Scope | File | | :---- | :--- | | User | `~/.claude/settings.json` | | Project (shared) | `.claude/settings.json` | | Project (private) | `.claude/settings.local.json` | | Managed | macOS: `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/`
Linux/WSL: `/etc/claude-code/`
Windows: `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\` | ```json { "model": "sonnet", "theme": "dark", "autoUpdatesChannel": "stable", "permissions": { "defaultMode": "default" } } ``` Settings precedence is **managed policy → CLI arguments/`--settings` → local → project → user**. Permission arrays have their own merge rules, so read the [settings reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings) before relying on ordinary last-writer-wins behavior. `~/.claude.json` stores global state, session/trust data, and local/user MCP configuration; it is not the user settings file.

Configuration Files

Claude Code combines human-authored instructions from several locations: | Memory Type | Location | Purpose | Use Case Examples | Shared With | | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | | **Enterprise policy** | macOS: `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md`
Linux: `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md`
Windows: `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md` | Organization-wide instructions managed by IT/DevOps | Company coding standards, security policies, compliance requirements | All users in organization | | **Project memory** | `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Team-shared instructions for the project | Project architecture, coding standards, common workflows | Team members via source control | | **User memory** | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Personal preferences for all projects | Code styling preferences, personal tooling shortcuts | Just you (all projects) | | **Project memory (local)** | `./CLAUDE.local.md` | Personal project-specific preferences (git-ignored) | Your sandbox URLs, preferred test data, personal overrides | Just you (current project) | | **Project rules** | `.claude/rules/**/*.md` | Modular project rules (loaded alongside CLAUDE.md) | Linting rules, API conventions, path-scoped standards | Team members via source control | > Instruction files are concatenated rather than overriding one another. User and ancestor-project files load at startup; `CLAUDE.md` files in subdirectories load lazily when Claude works there. `CLAUDE.md` is context, not an enforcement boundary. Use `@path` to import another file. Claude Code does not load `AGENTS.md` automatically; add `@AGENTS.md` to `CLAUDE.md` (or use a symlink where portable) when you want to share those instructions. #### `.claude/rules/` Directory The `.claude/rules/` directory lets you break project instructions into separate Markdown files instead of one large `CLAUDE.md`. Markdown files are discovered recursively. Add `paths` frontmatter with glob patterns when a rule should load only for matching files. This is useful for: - **Modular organization**: Separate concerns (e.g., `api-conventions.md`, `testing-rules.md`) - **Per-directory overrides**: Nested `rules/` directories can apply scoped rules - **Team collaboration**: Different team members can own different rule files via PR review #### Auto-Memory Claude can save useful working context under `~/.claude/projects//memory/`. It loads the first 200 lines or 25 KB of `MEMORY.md`; use `/memory` to inspect, edit, disable, or remove saved memories. Auto-memory is machine-local and shared across worktrees for the same repository. Auto-memory is most useful for context you would otherwise repeat across sessions: - Preferred build, test, and lint commands - Local conventions that are not obvious from code alone - Architecture decisions that influence future edits - Team preferences that should shape how Claude proposes changes Keep durable team rules in `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/rules/`. Treat auto-memory as helpful working context, not as the only source of truth. ---

repository.readme:
# 随行 Suixing

手机端的 AI Agent。给它一个 OpenAI 兼容的模型接口，它就能读你的屏幕、点你的手机、改你的文件、跑你的命令、按时提醒你。

> 0.7.0 起项目从「灵枢 / Lingshu」更名为「随行 / Suixing」，包名同步从 `com.lingshu.agent` 改为 `com.suixing.agent`。**包名变了意味着这是一次全新安装**：旧版本请先卸载，会话记录与设置不会迁移。

> ⚠️ **0.8.317 起会话存储格式变了，旧版本读不了新数据。** 会话从「一个 `<id>.json` 单文件、每次保存全量重写」改成「`chats/store/<id>.meta` + `<id>.<gen>.jsonl` 追加日志」。收益是 30 MB 的会话每轮保存从「重写 30 MB」降到「追加几十字节」。代价是**装回 0.8.316 及更早版本看不到这些会话**。本项目是单人自用的 beta，不做向后兼容；旧数据会在首次启动时由 `migratePending()` 逐个迁移（校验通过才退休旧文件，失败则原样保留、下次再试）。

- 纯 Kotlin + Jetpack Compose（Material 3），没有 NDK 源码；随包只带两个预编译的静态 shell 二进制（bash / BusyBox，见[第三方声明](#开源许可与第三方声明)）
- 目标平台：Android 8.0 (API 26) 及以上；`compileSdk` / `targetSdk` = 35
- 不做云同步、不做遥测，API Key 只存在本机应用私有目录
- 支持 MCP：任何 MCP 服务器提供的工具都会并进模型可调用的工具表
- 支持技能（Skill）：把写好的操作手册放进手机，模型需要时自己读
- 支持插件（Plugin）：安装一个 zip 就能带来新工具、新的上下文注入与新的执行闸门
- 当前源码版本：**0.8.300**（`versionCode` 311）

## 界面与设计

视觉取舍参考了 [Aether 扶摇](https://github.com/Zhou-Shilin/Aether)——不跟随 Material 动态取色、层级靠表面阶梯而不是阴影、卡片走大圆角、整页 edge-to-edge；布局与交互为本项目自研。随行自己的配色是一套手调的**墨绿**：深色侧底色 `#0F1412`、主色 `#8FD6B6`、正文 `#E8EFEA`，浅色侧白底 + 主色 `#1F6B4C`。几个刻意的选择：

- **不跟随 Material 动态取色**。默认用一套手调的「随行配色」，想要跟壁纸就在「设置 → 外观 → 配色」里切到「跟随壁纸」（Android 12 以上，会改用系统动态取色）。
- **不用阴影**。层级靠表面阶梯（`surfaceContainerLow` / `surfaceContainer` / `surfaceContainerHigh`，另有两级 Lowest / Highest）加 1dp 发丝描边区分。
- **卡片 20dp 圆角、左侧抽屉导航**。没有底部导航条，会话页的纵向空间全部留给消息；顶栏左上角的按钮拉出抽屉（会话列表 + 助手 / 定时任务 / 文件 / 悬浮窗控制台 / 设置）。
- **edge-to-edge**。状态栏与导航栏透明，内容自己处理 insets；顶栏自带 `statusBarsPadding()`，页面与输入框自带 `navigationBarsPadding()`。
- 会话页空状态是一个品牌标记加四条建议提示词（「看看现在屏幕上是什么」等），点一下直接填进输入框。
- 输入框那一行常驻一枚**模型胶囊**（当前模型名 + 思考强度徽标），点开是一张两页的卡：第一页是当前模型与思考强度滑杆，第二页是按端点、再按上游厂商分组的模型列表。
- **折叠块展开/收起时钉住块顶边**。思考过程、工具条展开时，用同一套逐帧补偿把块顶边按在原位，内容往下长而不是把上面的东西顶走。
- 切会话时转录有一次 **260ms** 的入场：淡入 + 从下方 24dp 升起 + 缩放落定。
- 外观页可调主题（跟随系统 / 浅色 / 深色）、配色、字号、圆角、气泡宽度、打字机效果、边缘光、提示条停留时间。

## 功能

### 对话

- **多会话**：左侧抽屉顶部是会话列表，支持改名、置顶、归档、导出、删除；默认只渲染最近 12 轮，顶部可以「加载更早的 12 轮」。
- **流式输出**：正文、思考、工具调用分三路流式回来，思考段与工具段会把正文段切开，合并回一条回复里。
- **Markdown 渲染**（自研实现，不依赖第三方库）：标题、有序 / 无序列表（支持嵌套）、表格、引用、代码块（含语言标签与复制按钮）、分割线、行内的加粗 / 斜体 / 删除线 / 行内代码、可点链接与自动识别的裸链接、文件路径可点。
- **前台服务保活**：`AgentForegroundService` 在任务运行期间挂一条常驻通知（通知渠道「任务执行」），切后台不中断。
- **思考过程折叠块**：推理模型（DeepSeek-R1 系、国产网关的 `reasoning_content`）的思考实时流出来，包在「思考过程」折叠条里。
  - 正在流的那一块**总是展开**（看着它长出来正是用推理模型的意义）；结束后按「设置 → 对话配置 → 历史思考块展开」决定，默认收起。
  - 点标题逐块展开/收起，选择按会话记住。
  - 整段思维链**逐行**渲染在一张倒序虚拟列表里（几千行也不会把主列表拖慢），高度上限默认 180dp，可在「设置 → 对话配置 → 思考块高度」调成 240 / 320。
  - 流式时自动追尾，手指往上拖就停跟，真滚到底再跟回来（「思考块跟随最新」可关）。
- **工具条**：一轮里跑的**所有工具合成一张卡**，头部写「调用 N 个工具」与失败数，每行一个工具，每个工具**各自**点开看详情。
  - 详情里有入参（等宽字体、不截断）、一条分割线、「输出」标签与复制按钮、输出逐行进虚拟列表，以及工具返回的截图。
  - 工具条本身是普通 `Column`（不做虚拟列表、不设高度上限，所以不会被截断），只有单个工具的详情保留 180dp 上限。
- **每条回复下方有 token 统计**：入 / 出 / 思考 / 缓存命中 / 耗时 / 输出速度（tok/s），接口没返回 usage 时这一行不显示；「用时详情」「用量详情」可展开成卡片。
- **上下文圆环**：输入框那一行的圆环显示当前对话占上下文窗口的比例，填了上下文窗口才显示比例，快满时变红。
- **发送图片**（多模态模型可直接看图；用纯文本模型时请保持设置里「模型支持图片输入」关闭，否则带图请求会被接口拒绝）；附件也可以是文件。
- **语音输入**：默认关闭。打开后输入框旁出现麦克风，走随行自己的录音链路（AudioRecord → WAV → 你配置的 OpenAI 兼容 `/audio/transcriptions`），**不弹系统识别面板**；失败时可手动降级到系统识别。
- **语音输出**：「朗读回复」打开后，每条回复结束用系统 TTS 读出；模型也能自己调 `speak` 工具主动说话。
- **消息可改**：长按任意一条（或点它下面的「修改」）就地编辑。用户消息可以「只保存」也可以「重新发送」——重新发送会丢掉这条之后的所有内容并让模型重新回答；助手回复只能改文字。
- **消息分叉**：对最后一个问题点「重新回答」，新答案作为**另一个候选**追加在同一个问题上，不覆盖旧的；气泡下方的 `‹ 1/2 ›` 式切换器在候选之间来回切，切换只改显示，后面的对话都留着。
- **停止 / 插话**：运行中发送键变「停止」，点停即停（不等当前工具跑完）；输入框里有内容时它变成「插话发送」，在下一个模型边界把这句话插进同一轮。插话可以排队（插话方式：排队 / 立即）。
- **任务清单**：模型调 `todo_write` 时，输入框上方出现一条待办行（`已完成/总数`），点它可以展开完整清单；完成的条目从行上消失，跑完或停止整条收起。
- **自动跟随**：在底部时新回复自动滚到底，上滑看历史就暂停跟随，出现「回到最新」按钮。
- **右侧轮次导航条**：一键在最近 6 轮之间跳转，往上拉可以解锁更早的轮次。

**助手（人设）**

抽屉里的「助手」一行打开半屏助手面板（设置 → 数据 → 助手设置 是同一份内容的整页）。每个助手有自己的名字、头像、一句话说明、系统提示词、模型、可选的单独温度，以及一份工具开关。

所有字段都是**加法**：留空的项跟随当前设置，所以只改个名字也能用。

| 字段 | 留空时 |
| --- | --- |
| 名字 / 头像 / 一句话说明 | 只影响显示 |
| 系统提示词 | 用设置页的系统提示词 |
| 模型 | 用当前模型（也可以钉死某个模型或某个提供方） |
| 温度 | 跟随全局温度（打开「单独设置温度」才用滑块的值） |
| 工具 | 全部可用（在助手的编辑页里把不想给的取消勾选） |

面板里点卡片＝切换，点右上角铅笔＝编辑；至少要留一个助手，所以最后一个删不掉（会直接告诉你为什么）。头像是可以用系统照片选择器上传的（不需要存储权限），会自动缩到 256px 存进私有目录，消息卡、流式气泡、空状态、助手列表都跟着变。模型也可以自己调 `create_assistant` 新建一个助手。

### 工具

内置 **50 个工具**，分 12 个工具包；分组由工具包自己声明，加一个工具、删一个工具，分组和人数自动跟着变。

| 分组 | 数量 | 工具 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 系统 | 10 | `device_info` `list_apps` `open_app` `open_url` `clipboard_read` `clipboard_write` `memory_write` `memory_read` `profile_write` `profile_read` |
| 文件 | 6 | `read_file` `write_file` `edit_file` `list_dir` `find_files` `grep_files`（前三个与 `list_dir`/`find_files`/`grep_files` 都在应用内执行，不 fork 进程；`mkdir`/`stat`/`mv`/`rm` 直接用 `run_shell`） |
| 界面操作 | 11 | `ui_dump` `ui_screenshot` `ui_tap` `ui_long_press` `ui_swipe` `ui_click_text` `ui_type` `ui_type_into` `ui_key` `ui_current_app` `ui_wait` |
| 后台任务 | 4 | `job_start` `job_list` `job_output` `job_kill` |
| 定时提醒 | 4 | `schedule_create` `schedule_list` `schedule_update` `schedule_delete` |
| 技能 | 4 | `skill_list` `skill_read` `skill_save` `skill_download` |
| 网络 | 3 | `web_fetch` `web_download` `web_search` |
| 任务清单 | 2 | `todo_write` `todo_read` |
| 语音 | 2 | `speak` `stop_speaking` |
| Shell | 2 | `run_shell` `app_action`（start / force_stop / clear_data / uninstall / disable / enable / info / permissions / install） |
| 其它（未声明分组） | 1 | `create_assistant` |
| 会话 | 1 | `get_session_status` |

- 另有引擎自己拦截的**虚拟工具** `compress_context`（手动压缩上下文），以及动态接入的 MCP 工具 `mcp__服务器名__工具名` 与插件工具 `<插件id>_<工具名>`。
- `get_session_status` 让模型随时能问「现在用的是哪个模型、哪个接口、上下文窗口多大、当前助手是谁、会话总数多少」——它是**只读**的，不碰会话内容。
- 文件工具的默认工作目录是 `Android/data/com.suixing.agent/files`（应用外部私有目录，不需要任何存储权限）；`~` 即该目录，绝对路径原样使用，相对路径里带 `..` 直接拒绝。
- 工具输出太长会被「溢写」到 `filesDir/toolout/`（保留头部，附一条让模型改用 `read_file` 去读的提示），不撑爆上下文。
- **工具审批**三档：自动运行 / 每次询问（默认）/ 禁止。被记住的「总是允许」与「总是拒绝」都可在一键清除。
- **并行工具数**可调（默认串行）；只有「自动运行」档才并行，「每次询问」档一次只问一个。
- 界面操作类工具走无障碍通道，Shell 类工具走 shell 通道，权限档次见下。

**联网**：`web_fetch` 抓网页（HTML 自动转纯文本，带编码嗅探，1MB 上限）、`web_download` 存文件到本机、`web_search` 搜网页。搜索默认走内置的 DuckDuckGo 抓取，零配置但容易被限流；想要稳定就在「设置 → 网络与语音」里填一个 Tavily 兼容接口（地址 + Key），`web_search` 会自动改走它。

### 模型

接口只要兼容 OpenAI 的 `/chat/completions` 就能用（DeepSeek、通义、Kimi、OpenRouter、vLLM、Ollama、局域网自建反代都行）。另外两种协议也在同一处选：**Anthropic Messages**（`/v1/messages`）与 **OpenAI Responses**（`/responses`）。

**多个接口**：一个地址一个「提供方」，设置页顶部用胶囊切换，`新建` 加一个、`删除` 去掉当前这个。切换提供方等于把它设为当前接口——地址、Key、模型一起换过去，不用来回改。

**不用手打模型名**：填好接口地址和 Key，点「获取模型列表」，随行会去请求 `{地址}/models`，把返回的模型按上游厂商分组列出来（聚合反代返回的 `deepseek/deepseek-chat`、`openai/gpt-4o` 会自动归到 `deepseek`、`openai` 两组，没有前缀的归到「其他」）。**可以多选**，每组还能一键全选；勾中的模型才会出现在模型切换器里。

- **地址写 `.../v1` 就行**，不用补 `/chat/completions`；补了也认。
- **局域网自签名证书**：如果你的反代是 `https://192.168.x.x:端口/v1` 这类自签证书，安卓会以 `Trust anchor for certification path not found` 拒绝。打开「设置 → 模型与生成 → 允许自签名证书」即可放行（只对模型请求生效，且只跳过证书校验，不影响别的）。更省事的办法是把地址写成 `http://`（应用已允许明文流量），或者在手机上把该证书装进系统信任库。
- **报错说人话**：401 会说「API Key 不对或已失效」，404 会提醒地址要以 `/v1` 结尾，连不上会说「检查地址和网络」，证书问题会直接告诉你打开上面那个开关；被截断的流会明确说「这一轮超过 10 分钟被中断」。
- **失败自动重试**（默认开）：只对连接重置、超时、5xx 与 429 重试，429 优先用服务端的 `Retry-After`；已经开始输出正文就绝不重试（那会重复计费）；用户点停止立刻结束等待。
- **上下文自动压缩**：上下文接近窗口上限时（阈值 20%–95%，默认 80%）把较早的对话压成摘要，摘要只进请求不落盘。也可以在输入框的「+」里手动「压缩上下文」。

**生成参数**（设置页「模型与生成」）——这几个都是加法：留默认就跟随接口自己的行为。

| 项 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| 显示思考过程 | 只控制画不画。关掉不代表不让模型思考，思考强度照旧生效 |
| 思考强度 | 对应接口的 `reasoning_effort`，七档：默认 / minimal / 低 / 中 / 高 / xhigh / max。不支持的模型会忽略这一项 |
| 上下文窗口（tokens） | 这个模型一次能读多少 token，可写 `128k` / `1m`；留空＝不限。填了，输入框那行的圆环才按比例显示 |
| 上下文条数 | 每次请求只带最近多少条消息，默认不限。历史很长时调小可以明显提速、省钱 |
| Top P | 核采样，1.00 表示不过滤，一般不用动 |
| 最大输出 tokens | 留空 = 模型默认。有些接口不给上限会中途截断，填上更稳 |

温度在「模型与生成」卡片里；每个助手还可以单独覆盖温度与提示词。模型切换器里的思考强度滑杆是**按会话**记的，不会把别的会话也改了。

### 扩展

「工具」页有四个标签：**工具 / 技能 / MCP / 插件**。

**工具**页是只读总览：可以搜索、看每个工具的名字、用途和它需要的权限；全局没有「禁用某个工具」的开关，唯一的禁用名单是按助手存的（去那个助手的编辑页取消勾选）。

**MCP（外挂工具）** 可以接入任意 [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) 服务器，接入后它提供的工具会和内置工具并列出现在模型面前，同样走审批闸门。两种传输方式：

| 传输 | 填什么 | 适用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stdio` | 一条启动命令，如 `python /sdcard/mcp/server.py` | 服务器是个本地进程，随行把它当子进程跑，用管道收发换行分隔的 JSON-RPC |
| `http` | 服务器地址，如 `http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp` | 服务器跑在 Termux、电脑或公网上（兼容 `streamable HTTP` 与 SSE 响应） |

- 工具名形如 `mcp__服务器名__工具名`，超长会自动截断并加短哈希防撞名（OpenAI 的函数名上限 64 字符）。
- 连接断了会后台指数退避重连（2s 起、最多 5 次），期间工具调用会返回「MCP 连接中断，正在后台重连」。
- 关于 stdio 的现实约束：安卓上子进程以应用自己的身份运行，读不到 Termux 的私有目录（`/data/data/com.termux` 是 0700）。所以手机本机跑 stdio 服务器有两条实用路径——把脚本放在应用能读的位置（如 `/sdcard`），或者设备已 root 时用 `su -c "node /data/local/tmp/server.js"` 借 root 跑。跑在 Termux 里的服务器更推荐走 `http`。
- 「测试」按钮会用一次性连接做完整握手（initialize → tools/list）并报出服务名、协议版本与工具数量，不会注册任何东西。

**技能（外挂知识）** 是写给模型看的操作手册——一段固定流程、一套规范、某个 App 的用法。和 MCP 的区别在于：MCP 给的是**工具**，技能给的是**怎么做**。

放在 `Android/data/com.suixing.agent/files/skills/` 下，两种形态都认：

```
skills/
├── daily-checkin/SKILL.md      # 一个文件夹一个技能
└── 修图规范.md                  # 或直接放一个 .md 文件
```

`SKILL.md` 的格式是 frontmatter + 正文：

```markdown
---
name: 每日签到
description: 打开某 App 完成签到，用户说「签到」时使用
---

1. 用 open_app 打开「XX」
2. 用 ui_dump 找到「签到」按钮并 ui_click_text 点击
3. 用 ui_dump 确认结果，截图回报
```

**为什么装很多也不占上下文**：系统提示词里只放技能的名字和 `description`，正文要用时由模型调用 `skill_read` 现读。所以 `description` 要写清「什么时候用」，模型才判断得出来。

「工具 → 技能」页可以查看全文、逐个开关、从系统文件管理器导入一个文件夹（批量）或一个 `.md`、从链接导入（超过 2 MB 的文件自动跳过）。导入的技能**默认关闭**，看过内容再打开开关；模型自己用 `skill_save` 存出来的技能默认开启。

**插件** 是一个 zip 包（包里有 `manifest.json` 和若干文件；选文件时选任意文件都行，由校验器判断它是不是插件）。装上去之前会先校验并把「会执行的内容」逐条摆出来给你确认；装好后可以单独开关、填它需要的环境变量（密钥写进 `env.json`，权限 0600）、看它注入了什么上下文、随时卸载（卸载进回收区，保留 7 天）。

- 清单字段：`id` / `version` / `displayName` / `description` / `author` / `env` / `tools` / `hooks` / `context` / `deps`。
- 命名规则：`id` 小写字母开头、只含小写字母 / 数字 / 横杠、≤32 字、不含点号；工具名同规则但可含下划线；注册名是 `<id>_<tool>`。
- 工具的执行方式只有两种：`http`（自定义请求模板）或 `shell`（本地命令，可声明需要 root）。
- 钩子目前只有 `tools/pre-execute` 一个事件，可以否决、要求确认或只记一条日志。
- 上下文注入支持 `{{device.model}}` `{{device.battery}}` `{{device.storage_free}}` `{{time.now}}` `{{foreground.app}}` 这几个变量。
- 插件按能力分四级：L1 只有说明、L2 带 `INSTRUCTIONS.md`、L3 带脚本或资源、L4 有依赖。

### 系统

**四档能力**（对应「能力」页的四张卡）——四档是叠加的：标准档人人都有，拿到 Shizuku 就自动拥有无障碍的能力，root 又覆盖前两档。

| 档位 | 获取方式 | 能做什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 标准档（默认） | 装上就有，不需要任何授权 | 聊天、记忆、待办、定时、技能、网络与文件工具 |
| 无障碍 | 系统设置里打开「随行 · 屏幕操作」 | 读屏（UI 树 dump）、截图、点击、长按、滑动、输入文本、按键 |
| Shizuku（ADB 级） | 安装 [Shizuku](https://shizuku.rikka.app/) 并授权随行 | 以 `shell` 身份执行 `am` / `pm` / `input` / `dumpsys` / `screencap` 等，可读写 `Android/data` 与 `/sdcard` |
| Root | 设备已 root | `su -c` 执行任意命令，直接读写系统文件 |

- 执行档次可以固定（「点已选中的那一档可回到自动」）。固定某一档时只走那一档，不可用时只向下退，绝不偷偷升到 root。
- 能力探测的结果会落盘：冷启动不再触发 superuser 弹窗，只有缓存不存在或你点「检测」时才重探。Shizuku 与无障碍的状态在回到前台时刷新。
- 没开也不会崩——相关工具会返回「权限不足 + 怎么开」的提示。
- 「所有文件访问权限」是另一条独立的授权，用来在文件页访问 `/sdcard`；拿不到时可以用 Shizuku 或 root 走全盘。

**悬浮窗控制台**：agent 跑起来时，屏幕上有一个可拖动的悬浮球，点开是一块面板，显示当前跑到哪了，有「停止」按钮和一个插话输入框，还能「回到对话」。抽屉里那一行既是开关也是授权入口。

**任务清单**：模型做多步任务时把步骤记下来，分「进行中 / 待办 / 已完成」；聊天页输入框上方的待办行点开就是完整清单。

**定时任务**：到点自己跑的一条提醒。`SchedulerService` 一次只挂一个闹钟（最近的那条），响完重排；开机、校时、换时区、换包之后都会重新排。错过的一次性提醒会标成「已过期」，不会补响。

**记忆**（模型在任务里主动记下的键值对）与**用户画像**（模型定期从对话里读出来的滚动摘要，`filesDir/profile.md`）是两回事：前者由模型自己决定记什么，后者按「画像整理间隔」定期重写，并且每次请求都注入提示词。画像页可以手动改，也可以「重新总结」。

**用量**页给的是 token：累计 tokens、会话数、最长单轮、近 30 天的每日柱状图、按模型的分布。

**性能**页分三段：最近若干轮的首字延迟 / 整轮耗时 / 缓存命中 / 输出速度均值；设备实时（CPU、GPU、帧率、内存、Java 堆、线程）；会话健康（p50 / p90、抖动、无 usage 回报的轮数、慢轮）。

**文件**页可以浏览三个根：工作目录（`Android/data/com.suixing.agent/files`）、`/sdcard`（需要「所有文件访问权限」）、插件目录。支持面包屑导航、上一级、刷新、文本预览与复制（预览上限 20KB）。这一页是只读的——要改文件走工具。

**会话管理**可以打开、导出（SAF 选位置，导出 JSON）、删除会话。

## 构建与出包

需要 **JDK 17** 与 Android SDK（`platforms;android-35`，以及与它配套的 build-tools 35.x）。SDK 路径写在 `local.properties` 的 `sdk.dir`（该文件不入库）。

**仓库刻意不带 `gradlew` / `gradlew.bat` / `gradle-wrapper.jar`**（从未被 git 跟踪），所以本地要用一个已解包的 Gradle 发行版，版本与 CI 对齐（**8.11+**）。CI 用 `gradle/actions/setup-gradle` 指定 8.11.1。

```bash
# 只查语法，不出包
gradle :app:compileDebugKotlin

# 单元测试（协议层往返、HTML 转纯文本、Markdown 解析、接口报错翻译、
# 提供方与模型分组、消息分叉的选取逻辑等，无需设备）
gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest

# 出包（只出 release）
gradle :app:assembleRelease
# 产物 app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
```

- 本机（Windows）没有 `gradle` 也不在 PATH 时，用一个**转发脚本**把 `gradlew.bat` 指到已解包的 Gradle 8.11.1（脚本只做一件事：设好 `JAVA_HOME` / `GRADLE_USER_HOME` 后 `call` 真实的 `gradle.bat %*`），任何 gradle 任务都能透传。转发脚本放在仓库之外，不入库。
- **出包纪律**：只出 release，不构建 debug——debug 的 `applicationId` 带 `.debug` 后缀，装上去会变成另一个应用。打包要等放行。
- 装机前必须 `aapt dump badging` 核对 APK 的 `versionName` / `versionCode`（历史上出过一次「构建没跑、把旧包当新包装机」的事故；几个版本的 APK 字节数完全相同，光看大小分不出来）。发错了用 `gh release upload --clobber` 覆盖附件。
- 推送到 GitHub 后 `.github/workflows/android.yml` 会自动跑：`gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest` → 上传测试报告 → `gradle :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleRelease` → 上传 `suixing-debug` / `suixing-release` 两个 APK artifact。
- release 用仓库内的 `app/sideload.keystore` 自签（alias / 密码均为 `lingshu`）——这是自用侧载包，不是上架包；该 keystore 必须入库，否则覆盖安装会失败。release 目前不开 minify（`isMinifyEnabled = false`），`proguard-rules.pro` 里的规则是为将来开混淆准备的。

## 首次使用

**第一次打开会有一个引导页**（五页，可随时跳过）：欢迎 → 选供应商并填接口与 Key → 选模型与思考
强度 → 权限（按「要做什么 → 需要什么 → 缺了会怎样」讲）→ 开始使用。里面预置了 DeepSeek、智谱
GLM、OpenAI 兼容（自填地址）、本机 Ollama、Kimi、千问、硅基流动、Claude 八个接口，点一下就
预填地址与模型名。

跳过也没关系——没配 Key 一样能先逛逛，聊天会等你配好接口。**「设置 → 数据与关于 → 新手引导」**
可以随时再看一遍。

不用引导页的话，手动配也一样：

1. 安装 APK，打开「随行」
2. 「设置 → 模型与生成」→ 填接口地址（如 `https://api.deepseek.com/v1`）、API Key → 点「获取模型列表」，勾选要用的模型（可多选，按上游厂商分组）→「测试连接」→「保存」（局域网自签证书见上一节）
3. 「能力」→ 打开无障碍服务（不开也能聊，但用不了 UI 自动化）；想要 ADB 级能力就装 Shizuku 并授权
4. 回会话页，直接说人话，例如「打开微信，给文件传输助手发一条『你好』」

> **API Key 存在哪**：用系统 Keystore（AES/GCM）加密后存在这台手机上，密钥不随应用数据走 ⇒
> 换机后需要重填一次。这是「更保密」与「换机免重填」之间的取舍，取前者。

## 已知限制

- 无障碍截图需要 Android 11 (API 30) 及以上；低版本 `ui_screenshot` 会返回失败提示
- 国产 ROM 可能把第三方应用加进无障碍黑名单（vivo/OriginOS 等），此时无障碍工具不可用
- 安卓 16+ 的「高级保护模式」会拦截未知来源安装并限制无障碍，请勿开启
- Shizuku 在设备重启后需要重新启动（无线调试或 root 方式）
- stdio 方式的 MCP 服务器读不到 Termux 的私有目录（见上面 MCP 一节）

- 功能设计参照了 [Operit](https://github.com/AAswordman/Operit)（LGPL-3.0）与 [Aether 扶摇](https://github.com/Zhou-Shilin/Aether)（GPL-3.0）的能力清单与交互约定，视觉取值参考了后者。本项目为独立实现，未复制上述项目的源代码。
- 应用内「设置 → 关于」页里有指向本仓库、发布页、问题反馈与构建说明的链接，以及上面这些项目的出处。
